usage_note_en: 悪役 literally means the 'bad role.' It can refer to the character, the role in a production, or someone made to appear blameworthy.
contrast: 敵役: an opposing role, not necessarily morally evil
黒幕: the hidden mastermind behind events
example_ja_2: 彼は舞台で悪役を演じた。
example_en_2: He played the villain on stage.
misuse_note_en: An antagonist is not always an 悪役. Use 敵役 when the character merely opposes the protagonist without being morally villainous.

example_ja: 主人公とライバルキャラが決勝でぶつかる。
example_en: The protagonist and the rival character meet in the final.
speaker_image: A fan, reviewer, or creator describing a character built around competition with another.
real_life_use: Common in casual media talk. ライバル alone works both for fictional and real competitors; キャラ makes the media framing explicit.
usage_note_en: A ライバルキャラ challenges the protagonist or another central character and may be ally, enemy, or both over the story.
contrast: 敵キャラ: enemy character, with no requirement of equal competition
宿敵: long-standing or fated archrival with stronger dramatic weight
example_ja_2: あのライバルキャラは途中から仲間になる。
example_en_2: That rival character joins the group partway through.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every opponent as a rival. A rival usually has an ongoing comparative relationship with the central character.

example_ja: 公式サイトでキャラクター人気投票が始まった。
example_en: A character popularity poll has opened on the official website.
speaker_image: A publisher, fan, or participant ranking characters, works, or products by votes.
real_life_use: Standard beyond fandom as well. Add the target before 人気投票, such as キャラクター人気投票 or 楽曲人気投票.
usage_note_en: 人気投票 collects votes about popularity, not necessarily quality. Results may be used for rankings, promotions, or bonus projects.
contrast: ランキング: the resulting or published ranking
総選挙: large-scale vote, often promotional and more event-like
example_ja_2: 人気投票では脇役が一位になった。
example_en_2: A supporting character took first place in the popularity poll.
misuse_note_en: Do not call a sales chart 人気投票 unless people actually cast votes; popularity measured by purchases is a ranking, not a poll.

en: tsundere; initially cold but secretly affectionate type
example_ja: 彼女は素直になれないツンデレキャラとして人気がある。
example_en: She is popular as a tsundere character who cannot express her feelings honestly.
speaker_image: A fan classifying a fictional character by a familiar personality pattern.
real_life_use: Widely recognized in fandom and broader pop culture. Applying it to a real person can oversimplify or excuse unfriendly behavior.
usage_note_en: ツンデレ combines ツンツン, aloof or prickly behavior, with デレデレ, openly affectionate behavior. The balance and timing vary by character.
contrast: クーデレ: outwardly cool and controlled but affectionate underneath
ヤンデレ: affection expressed through obsessive or dangerous behavior
example_ja_2: 最初は冷たかったのに、最近はデレが増えてきた。
example_en_2: She was cold at first, but lately her affectionate side has appeared more often.
misuse_note_en: Do not use the label as a clinical personality description. It is a character trope and does not justify disrespectful real-life conduct.

example_ja: いざというときに逃げるへたれキャラだ。
example_en: He is the kind of wimpy character who runs when it matters.
speaker_image: A fan or character mocking someone who lacks nerve, resolve, or competence.
real_life_use: Used outside fandom too, but insulting when applied to a real person. It can be self-deprecating in casual speech.
usage_note_en: へたれ describes someone who folds under pressure or fails to act courageously. It need not mean physically weak.
contrast: 臆病者: coward, focusing directly on fear
弱キャラ: weak character in game or story power terms
example_ja_2: 怖くなって戻ってきた自分がへたれすぎる。
example_en_2: I chickened out and came back. I'm pathetic.
misuse_note_en: Do not use it as a neutral character category. It carries ridicule and can insult a real person's courage or reliability.

example_ja: 未来が見えるなんて、完全にチート能力だ。
example_en: Being able to see the future is completely overpowered.
speaker_image: A gamer or fan judging an ability, item, or character unfairly powerful.
real_life_use: Common in games and fantasy discussion. In ordinary contexts チート may also mean literal cheating, so compounds and context matter.
usage_note_en: From English 'cheat,' fandom チート often describes power so strong that it feels like using a cheat code, even when no rule was broken.
contrast: 反則級: figuratively 'almost unfair' in strength or appeal
最強: simply the strongest, without the cheat-code implication
example_ja_2: 序盤でその装備を取るとチートになる。
example_en_2: Getting that equipment early makes the game unbalanced.
misuse_note_en: Do not infer actual dishonesty from チート能力. Conversely, チート行為 usually does refer to rule-breaking or cheating.

example_ja: 新加入の選手が一人で試合を無双した。
example_en: The new player dominated the match almost single-handedly.
speaker_image: A fan, player, or commentator excitedly describing overwhelming performance.
real_life_use: Used casually for games, sports, business, and other fields; avoid it in formal reporting unless quoting slang.
usage_note_en: Modern 無双する means to overpower everyone around you, based on 無双, 'without equal.' The natural object or setting is often marked with で rather than directly as 敵を無双する.
contrast: 圧勝する: win by a large margin
無敵: invincible as a state or quality
example_ja_2: このキャラを使えば序盤は無双できる。
example_en_2: With this character, you can steamroll the early game.
misuse_note_en: Avoid unnatural 敵を無双する as a default pattern. Say 戦場で無双する or 敵を圧倒する depending on the intended grammar.

en: awakening; newly unleashed awareness or power
example_ja: 追い詰められた主人公が新たな力に覚醒する。
example_en: Cornered, the protagonist awakens to a new power.
speaker_image: A narrator or fan describing a sudden breakthrough in power, talent, or consciousness.
real_life_use: The word exists outside fiction for awakening to an idea or from unconsciousness, but power-up use is dramatic and genre-coded.
usage_note_en: 覚醒 literally concerns waking or becoming aware. Fantasy and battle stories extend it to dormant abilities suddenly becoming active.
contrast: 目覚める: ordinary wakefulness or figurative awakening, less technical
開花する: talent or ability blossoms through development
example_ja_2: 事故のあと、患者はようやく覚醒した。
example_en_2: The patient finally regained consciousness after the accident.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume every 覚醒 is a supernatural power-up. Medical, spiritual, and ideological contexts use the same word differently.

example_ja: 現代の会社員が異世界に転生する物語だ。
example_en: It is a story about a modern office worker reincarnated in another world.
speaker_image: A narrator, reader, or believer discussing rebirth into another life or world.
real_life_use: Common as an isekai premise and also a genuine religious concept. Treat belief contexts respectfully rather than as fandom jargon.
usage_note_en: 転生 means being born again in a different life. Genre stories often specify the destination with に and the prior identity with から or a description.
contrast: 転移: transported to another world without being reborn
生まれ変わる: everyday phrasing for being born again or completely changing
example_ja_2: 彼は魔法使いの家に転生した。
example_en_2: He was reincarnated into a family of mages.
misuse_note_en: Do not confuse 転生 with simple transportation. If the same living body moves worlds, 異世界転移 is usually more precise.

example_ja: 現実世界と異世界を行き来する設定だ。
example_en: The premise lets the characters travel between the real world and another world.
speaker_image: A fan, publisher, or narrator referring to a world separate from ordinary reality.
real_life_use: Widely understood in media discussion. In English-language fandom, 'isekai' may name the genre rather than translate the noun.
usage_note_en: 異世界 literally means a different world. As a genre label it covers reincarnation, summoning, and transportation stories, but the word itself only names the setting.
contrast: 異次元: another dimension, often spatial or science-fictional
ファンタジー世界: a fantasy world without implying travel from our world
example_ja_2: 異世界ものばかり読んでいた時期がある。
example_en_2: There was a period when I read almost nothing but isekai stories.
misuse_note_en: Not every fantasy is 異世界もの. The label usually matters when another world is contrasted with the protagonist's original reality.

example_ja: 転生した主人公は鑑定のチートスキルを授かる。
example_en: The reincarnated protagonist receives an overpowered appraisal skill.
speaker_image: A fantasy or game fan describing an exceptionally advantageous ability.
real_life_use: Mostly genre discussion. スキル in Japanese media often means a named game-like ability, not general human competence.
usage_note_en: チートスキル combines the cheat-code sense of チート with a discrete game-style ability. It often signals wish-fulfillment or power-fantasy conventions.
contrast: 特殊能力: special ability without implying imbalance
固有スキル: unique skill belonging to a particular character
example_ja_2: そのチートスキルには一日一回という制限がある。
example_en_2: That overpowered skill can only be used once a day.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate Japanese スキル here as an ordinary learned skill such as writing or cooking; it is usually a system-defined ability.

en: shift into a battle-focused plot; battle development
example_ja: 交渉が決裂し、物語はバトル展開に入った。
example_en: The negotiations broke down, and the story shifted into a battle arc.
speaker_image: A fan or reviewer describing the plot moving toward combat.
real_life_use: Used in informal media discussion. It is descriptive fan shorthand, not a formal narrative-theory term.
usage_note_en: 展開 means the way events unfold. バトル展開 refers to a stretch or turn in which fighting becomes the plot's main engine.
contrast: 戦闘シーン: the actual scene depicting combat
急展開: any sudden plot development, not necessarily a battle
example_ja_2: 日常ものだと思ったら、急にバトル展開になった。
example_en_2: I thought it was a slice-of-life story, and then it suddenly turned into a battle series.
misuse_note_en: Avoid the literal English 'battle development.' Translate the narrative shift or sequence naturally for the sentence.

example_ja: 主人公が最後に必殺技を繰り出した。
example_en: The protagonist unleashed a signature finishing move at the end.
speaker_image: A narrator, fan, or child naming a character's decisive special technique.
real_life_use: Strongly associated with action fiction, games, and playful imitation. Figurative real-life use can mean someone's winning trick or specialty.
usage_note_en: Despite the characters 必殺, 'certain kill,' a 必殺技 does not have to kill. It is a named, decisive, or signature technique.
contrast: 奥義: secret or ultimate technique learned within an art
特殊技: special move without the same climactic force
example_ja_2: 彼の必殺技は営業先の名前を一度で覚えることだ。
example_en_2: His secret weapon in sales is remembering every client's name after hearing it once.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it rigidly as 'certain-kill technique.' 'Finishing move,' 'special attack,' or figurative 'secret weapon' often fits better.

en: death flag; sign a character may soon die
example_ja: 『帰ったら結婚する』は典型的な死亡フラグだ。
example_en: 'I'm getting married when I return' is a classic death flag.
speaker_image: A genre-savvy viewer noticing ominous foreshadowing based on familiar story patterns.
real_life_use: Used mainly as humorous media commentary and occasionally as a joke about risky real-life statements. Be tactful around actual danger or loss.
usage_note_en: A 死亡フラグ is a line, event, or character beat that conventionally foreshadows death. It predicts through trope recognition, not certainty.
contrast: 伏線: planted setup that later pays off
死亡予告: explicit notice or prediction of death
example_ja_2: 急に家族の話を始めて、死亡フラグっぽかった。
example_en_2: When he suddenly started talking about his family, it felt like a death flag.
misuse_note_en: Do not call every ominous scene a confirmed spoiler. A flag is a perceived convention and may be deliberately subverted.

en: a narrative flag is triggered; signs point toward an outcome
example_ja: 二人きりになって、恋愛フラグが立った。
example_en: Once they were alone together, it felt like a romance route had opened.
speaker_image: A fan interpreting an event as activating a likely future plot outcome.
real_life_use: Common in fandom and joking real-life narration. Specify the type—恋愛フラグ, 死亡フラグ, 負けフラグ—when context is unclear.
usage_note_en: Borrowed conceptually from programming and games, フラグが立つ means a condition appears to have been met for a later event.
contrast: 伏線が張られる: narrative setup is deliberately planted
フラグを回収する: the anticipated outcome or setup pays off
example_ja_2: その発言で裏切りフラグが立った気がする。
example_en_2: That line made me suspect a future betrayal.
misuse_note_en: A literal English 'flag was raised' may be opaque. Translate the predicted outcome or use established fandom 'flag' only for the right audience.

example_ja: 二人が黙って手をつなぐ場面の尊さにやられた。
example_en: The quiet scene where they hold hands was almost too precious to bear.
speaker_image: An emotionally invested fan praising a relationship, character, or moment as deeply precious.
real_life_use: Common in online fandom. Standard 尊さ can mean nobility or sacred value, while fandom use is hyperbolic and affective.
usage_note_en: The noun form of 尊い became fandom language for the overwhelming value of a beloved interaction or existence. English usually needs a freer rendering.
contrast: 尊い: adjective meaning precious, noble, or fandom 'too precious'
エモさ: emotionally evocative quality, often nostalgic or atmospheric
example_ja_2: 推しが楽しそうに笑っているだけで尊さを感じる。
example_en_2: Just seeing my favorite character smile happily feels precious.
misuse_note_en: Avoid translating it mechanically as 'preciousness' in polished English. Also distinguish fandom praise from religious or moral 尊さ.

example_ja: 最終話の手紙の場面で涙腺崩壊した。
example_en: The letter scene in the finale had me sobbing.
speaker_image: A fan exaggerating humorously that an emotional scene made them cry hard.
real_life_use: Common in reviews and social posts, not formal writing. It refers to the viewer's reaction or labels content as highly tear-inducing.
usage_note_en: Literally 'tear-duct collapse,' the compound is playful hyperbole. 涙腺崩壊する means to break down crying at emotional content.
contrast: 号泣する: actually sob loudly
泣ける: can make one cry; moving, with less hyperbole
example_ja_2: この動画は後半から涙腺崩壊だから、電車で見ないほうがいい。
example_en_2: The second half of this video is a total tearjerker, so don't watch it on the train.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate the anatomy literally as 'my tear ducts broke.' Render the emotional effect in natural English.

example_ja: 敵だった二人が共闘する神展開になった。
example_en: In a brilliant turn, the two former enemies joined forces.
speaker_image: An excited fan giving emphatic approval to the way a plot develops.
real_life_use: Common in casual reviews and social media. It is enthusiastic evaluation, not neutral description.
usage_note_en: 神 acts as a slang prefix meaning exceptional or god-tier. 神展開 praises a plot turn, reveal, or sequence as outstanding.
contrast: 急展開: sudden development without judging it good
胸熱展開: an emotionally rousing, hype-inducing development
example_ja_2: 伏線が全部つながる神展開だった。
example_en_2: It was an amazing payoff that connected every clue.
misuse_note_en: Do not render 神 literally as divine unless the context is religious. The phrase is strong fan praise and can sound exaggerated in formal criticism.

example_ja: 味方だと思っていた人物が黒幕だったという衝撃展開だ。
example_en: In a shocking turn, the person they trusted as an ally was the mastermind.
speaker_image: A fan or entertainment writer emphasizing a plot turn's shock value.
real_life_use: Used in informal media discussion and promotional copy. In formal criticism, describe the specific reveal rather than relying on the label.
usage_note_en: 衝撃 modifies 展開 to evaluate how events unfold. The phrase may refer to a reveal, reversal, loss, or any turn intended to stun the audience.
contrast: 急展開: events change suddenly, without necessarily being shocking
どんでん返し: a reversal that overturns the audience's understanding
example_ja_2: 予告なしの衝撃展開に、視聴者がざわついた。
example_en_2: The unannounced shock twist set viewers talking.
misuse_note_en: Avoid the wooden English 'shock development.' Translate what turned or was revealed, especially outside fandom writing.

en: sudden turn of events; rapid plot shift
example_ja: 主人公の逮捕をきっかけに、物語が急展開を迎える。
example_en: The protagonist's arrest sends the story in a sudden new direction.
speaker_image: A narrator, reviewer, or viewer describing events that begin changing quickly.
real_life_use: Common in news, sports, and real-life narration as well as fiction. It does not by itself judge the change good or bad.
usage_note_en: 急展開 can mean a sudden development in one event or a rapid succession of changes. 〜を迎える and 急展開する are common patterns.
contrast: 衝撃展開: stresses the audience's shock
急転: abrupt change, often in the fixed phrase 事態が急転する
example_ja_2: 交渉は午後になって急展開した。
example_en_2: The negotiations shifted dramatically in the afternoon.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 急展開 means a twist that reverses prior facts. It may simply mean that the pace or situation changes quickly.

example_ja: 放課後は毎日、吹奏楽部の部活がある。
example_en: I have wind ensemble practice every day after school.
speaker_image: A student, teacher, or fan discussing extracurricular school clubs and their activities.
real_life_use: Everyday school vocabulary. Depending on context, 部活 may mean the club itself, its scheduled practice, or club participation generally.
usage_note_en: Short for 部活動. Japanese school clubs often meet regularly and can structure a student's social life, which makes 部活 a common story setting.
contrast: サークル: usually a looser university or community group
クラブ活動: fuller term, also used for school activities
example_ja_2: 部活を引退してから、放課後の時間が増えた。
example_en_2: Since retiring from the school club, I've had more free time after class.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 部活 as a casual hobby club. It may involve frequent practice, competitions, and a formal 先輩後輩 structure.

example_ja: 文化祭でクラスのみんなと喫茶店を出す。
example_en: Our class is running a café at the school festival.
speaker_image: A student or teacher discussing a school event featuring class exhibits, performances, and food stalls.
real_life_use: Ordinary Japanese school vocabulary. University events may also be called 学園祭 or 大学祭.
usage_note_en: A 文化祭 is a school cultural festival, typically organized by students. Common fictional episodes use preparation, performances, and public visitors as social catalysts.
contrast: 体育祭: school sports festival
学園祭: broader campus festival term, especially common for universities
example_ja_2: 今年の文化祭では演劇部が二公演行う。
example_en_2: The drama club will give two performances at this year's school festival.
misuse_note_en: English 'culture festival' may be unclear without 'school.' Add the institutional context when writing for readers unfamiliar with Japan.

example_ja: 中学の修学旅行で京都と奈良を訪れた。
example_en: On our junior high school trip, we visited Kyoto and Nara.
speaker_image: A student, teacher, or former student discussing an organized educational trip by a school year group.
real_life_use: Standard real-life term. The trip is usually longer and more formally organized than an ordinary field trip.
usage_note_en: 修学旅行 is a major overnight school trip intended to combine education and group experience. The destination and timing differ by school.
contrast: 遠足: shorter excursion or field trip, often a day trip
研修旅行: training or study tour with an explicit instructional purpose
example_ja_2: 修学旅行の班を来週までに決める。
example_en_2: We have to choose our school-trip groups by next week.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it as a generic vacation. It is a school-organized trip with schedules, groups, and educational expectations.

example_ja: 彼とは幼なじみで、家も近い。
example_en: He and I have been friends since childhood, and our homes are close.
speaker_image: A character or real speaker describing someone known since childhood.
real_life_use: Ordinary vocabulary, not merely a romance trope. 幼なじみ is the common modern spelling; 幼馴染 is also seen.
usage_note_en: The term describes a relationship formed in childhood. It says nothing by itself about current closeness, gender, or romantic interest.
contrast: 同級生: person in the same school year or class
旧友: old friend, without specifying childhood
example_ja_2: 幼なじみだからこそ、素直に謝れない。
example_en_2: Precisely because we've known each other since childhood, I can't bring myself to apologize honestly.
misuse_note_en: Do not add romantic meaning automatically. Stories often use the trope romantically, but real 幼なじみ are simply childhood acquaintances or friends.

example_ja: 二学期の初日に、東京から転校生が来た。
example_en: A transfer student from Tokyo arrived on the first day of the second term.
speaker_image: A student, teacher, or narrator identifying someone who has transferred into a school.
real_life_use: Standard school vocabulary. 転入生 is a more administrative term for a student entering from another school.
usage_note_en: 転校生 focuses on the person's status as someone who changed schools. Fiction often uses the arrival to introduce a new social element or hidden past.
contrast: 転入生: incoming transfer student in administrative language
新入生: newly enrolled first-year student, not necessarily a transfer
example_ja_2: 転校生はまだ新しい制服が届いていない。
example_en_2: The transfer student's new uniform has not arrived yet.
misuse_note_en: Do not use 転校生 for an exchange student by default; 留学生 or 交換留学生 may be more accurate.

example_ja: 部活の下級生に道具の使い方を教えた。
example_en: I showed the younger club members how to use the equipment.
speaker_image: A student or member referring to someone in a lower school year or rank within the same institution.
real_life_use: Normal in schools and hierarchical groups. 後輩 is more relational: someone junior to the speaker, while 下級生 simply belongs to a lower grade.
usage_note_en: 下級生 is based on grade level. A third-year student can call first- and second-year students 下級生 regardless of personal acquaintance.
contrast: 後輩: junior relative to a particular senior
年下: younger in age, independent of school grade
example_ja_2: 下級生だった彼も、今年は最上級生だ。
example_en_2: He used to be an underclassman, but this year he is in the highest grade.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it as 'inferior student.' 下 refers to institutional grade, not ability or worth.

example_ja: あの部は先輩後輩の上下関係が厳しい。
example_en: That club has a strict hierarchy between senior and junior members.
speaker_image: A student, employee, or observer discussing rank based on entry year or experience.
real_life_use: Used well beyond fiction in schools, clubs, workplaces, and sports. The exact duties and language vary by organization.
usage_note_en: 先輩後輩 names the paired social structure, not two fixed personality types. A person can be one member's 先輩 and another's 後輩.
contrast: 上下関係: hierarchy more broadly
同級生: peers in the same school year
example_ja_2: 年齢より入社年で先輩後輩が決まることもある。
example_en_2: In some workplaces, seniority is based on when people joined rather than age.
misuse_note_en: Do not reduce the relationship to 'older versus younger.' Entry year, experience, and institutional membership often matter more than age.

example_ja: 親友二人が同じ人を好きになり、三角関係になる。
example_en: Two close friends fall for the same person, creating a love triangle.
speaker_image: A narrator or viewer describing romantic feelings involving three people.
real_life_use: Common in media and real-life gossip or relationship discussion. Use tactfully when referring to actual people.
usage_note_en: 三角関係 usually refers to romantic competition or overlapping affection among three people, though the exact directions of feeling vary.
contrast: 四角関係: similarly tangled relationship among four people
両片思い: two people like each other but neither realizes or confesses it
example_ja_2: 三角関係だと思っていたが、実は一人の勘違いだった。
example_en_2: What looked like a love triangle turned out to be one person's misunderstanding.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume all three people are dating. The term may describe only unspoken or one-sided feelings.

example_ja: 卒業式のあと、好きな人に告白した。
example_en: After graduation, I confessed my feelings to the person I liked.
speaker_image: A person openly disclosing romantic feelings, a secret, or wrongdoing.
real_life_use: Common. In romance, 好きな人に告白する is understood as confessing love; elsewhere the content must be stated.
usage_note_en: 告白 means revealing something personally significant. Media often narrows it to a romantic confession, but the word also covers secrets and admissions.
contrast: プロポーズ: proposal of marriage
自白: confession of a crime, especially in legal or police contexts
example_ja_2: 彼は記者会見で過去のうそを告白した。
example_en_2: At the press conference, he admitted that he had lied in the past.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 告白 as a love confession. Identify what is disclosed and to whom.

en: mutual crush with neither side aware
example_ja: 二人とも好きなのに気づいていない両片思いの状態だ。
example_en: They both have feelings for each other, but neither realizes it.
speaker_image: A fan or friend describing two people whose supposedly one-sided feelings are actually mutual.
real_life_use: Common in romance discussion and online fandom, but not a formal psychological or relationship term.
usage_note_en: 両 combines two instances of 片思い: each person believes or behaves as though the love is one-sided, even though the feelings match.
contrast: 片思い: one-sided love
両思い: mutual love recognized as such
example_ja_2: 両片思いが長すぎて、読者のほうがじれったくなる。
example_en_2: Their unspoken mutual crush lasts so long that readers get impatient.
misuse_note_en: Do not use it once both people have recognized and communicated their feelings; that is simply 両思い.

example_ja: かつてのライバルが助けに来る燃える展開だった。
example_en: It was a thrilling turn when the former rival arrived to help.
speaker_image: An excited fan praising a scene that sparks fighting spirit or emotional hype.
real_life_use: Common in casual reviews. 燃える can also literally burn or mean becoming passionately motivated, so the noun and context matter.
usage_note_en: 燃える展開 is not merely exciting. It evokes rising spirit: a comeback, alliance, sacrifice, or challenge that makes the audience want to cheer.
contrast: 胸熱展開: emotionally stirring or triumphant development
神展開: broadly judges a development excellent
example_ja_2: 劣勢から全員で立ち上がるのは燃える展開だ。
example_en_2: Seeing everyone rise together after falling behind is the kind of comeback that gets you fired up.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it literally as a plot that burns. Render the audience's excitement or the rousing turn.

example_ja: 付き合い始めた二人の甘々な日常が描かれる。
example_en: The story follows the couple's lovey-dovey daily life after they start dating.
speaker_image: A romance fan describing unusually affectionate dialogue, behavior, or atmosphere.
real_life_use: Used in fandom and casual product descriptions. It can praise sweetness or imply that it is excessive, depending on tone.
usage_note_en: Reduplicated 甘々 intensifies 甘い. In romance it means openly tender and low-conflict; in food it can mean extremely sweet.
contrast: ラブラブ: visibly in love as a couple
いちゃいちゃ: flirt or act physically affectionate, sometimes annoying observers
example_ja_2: 砂糖を入れすぎて、コーヒーが甘々になった。
example_en_2: I added too much sugar, and the coffee became extremely sweet.
misuse_note_en: Do not default to negative 'sickeningly sweet.' The phrase may be enthusiastic praise, and it also has a literal food meaning.

example_ja: 隣の部屋に新婚さんが引っ越してきた。
example_en: A newlywed couple moved into the apartment next door.
speaker_image: A host, neighbor, or acquaintance referring warmly to a recently married person or couple.
real_life_use: Common and friendly. 新婚夫婦 explicitly means a newly married couple; 新婚 is also used in compounds such as 新婚生活.
usage_note_en: さん adds a personable, sometimes TV-host-like warmth to 新婚. Depending on context, it may refer to one newlywed person or the couple as a unit.
contrast: 新婚夫婦: explicit newly married couple
夫婦: married couple without saying how recently
example_ja_2: 二人は新婚さんみたいに仲がいい。
example_en_2: Those two get along like newlyweds.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume people welcome questions about how 'newlywed' they are. The term is friendly but still concerns private relationship status.

example_ja: 二人の痴話喧嘩に友人まで巻き込まれた。
example_en: Even their friends got dragged into the couple's quarrel.
speaker_image: An observer characterizing a couple's private romantic dispute as petty or tiresome.
real_life_use: Used outside fiction, but it minimizes the dispute. Avoid it when there may be abuse, coercion, or serious harm.
usage_note_en: 痴話 refers to intimate talk between lovers; 痴話喧嘩 is their quarrel. The label often carries an outsider's amused or dismissive judgment.
contrast: 夫婦喧嘩: quarrel between spouses, without necessarily calling it trivial
口喧嘩: verbal argument between any people
example_ja_2: ただの痴話喧嘩だと思って、誰も止めに入らなかった。
example_en_2: Everyone assumed it was just a lovers' spat, so nobody intervened.
misuse_note_en: Do not use the term to dismiss threats or violence as a private couple matter. It is appropriate only when the conflict is genuinely minor.

example_ja: 仲間が次々に離れていく鬱展開が続く。
example_en: The story enters a bleak stretch as the companions leave one after another.
speaker_image: A fan labeling a story arc emotionally oppressive, tragic, or draining.
real_life_use: Common in casual media discussion, but 鬱 is also the everyday shorthand for depression. Use more precise language around actual mental health.
usage_note_en: In 鬱展開, 鬱 works as fandom shorthand for a deeply depressing sequence of events. The term evaluates the viewer's emotional burden, not a character's diagnosis.
contrast: シリアス展開: serious turn that need not be depressing
胸糞展開: upsetting because it feels cruel, unjust, or disgusting
example_ja_2: 中盤の鬱展開を越えると、少し希望が見えてくる。
example_en_2: After the bleak middle arc, the story finally offers some hope.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it as 'a depression plot' or use it to diagnose a person. Prefer 'bleak,' 'grim,' or 'depressing' for the narrative effect.

example_ja: 作画も脚本もすばらしくて、今期の神アニメだと思う。
example_en: The animation and writing are excellent; for me, it is the standout anime of the season.
speaker_image: An enthusiastic fan giving an anime the highest informal praise.
real_life_use: Common in posts and casual conversation. It is hyperbolic and subjective, so it does not suit neutral reviews without attribution.
usage_note_en: The slang prefix 神 means exceptional or god-tier. 神アニメ praises the work as a whole, though speakers may use it jokingly or impulsively.
contrast: 名作アニメ: acclaimed or enduring masterpiece, less slangy
覇権アニメ: title perceived to dominate a season's attention or sales
example_ja_2: 最終回まで見て、神アニメという評価に納得した。
example_en_2: After watching the finale, I understood why fans called it exceptional.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 神 literally as religious 'divine.' Also avoid presenting this fan judgment as an objective category.

example_ja: 彼は右目に特別な力があるという厨二病設定を作った。
example_en: He invented a chūnibyō persona in which his right eye has a special power.
speaker_image: A fan or peer teasing melodramatic adolescent fantasies, invented powers, or grandiose self-presentation.
real_life_use: Widely recognized slang. 厨二病 is an internet-styled spelling of 中二病 and is not a medical diagnosis.
usage_note_en: Literally 'second-year middle-school syndrome,' the joke targets behavior associated with early-adolescent self-dramatization. It is now also a deliberate character aesthetic.
contrast: 中二病: standard spelling of the same slang concept
邪気眼: a subtype centered on pretending to possess a hidden supernatural power
example_ja_2: 昔書いた必殺技の名前を見ると、中二病だったころを思い出す。
example_en_2: Seeing the special-move names I wrote reminds me of my chūnibyō phase.
misuse_note_en: Do not describe genuine delusions or mental illness with this label. It is teasing slang, not clinical vocabulary.

example_ja: 最後は仲間の声援を受けた友情パワーで逆転した。
example_en: In the end, support from the hero's friends inspired a comeback.
speaker_image: A fan praising or poking fun at friendship becoming a decisive source of strength.
real_life_use: Mostly used in story discussion and playful real-life encouragement. Tone determines whether it celebrates the trope or calls it convenient writing.
usage_note_en: 友情パワー makes an abstract bond behave like literal power. Battle stories may depict it as morale, cooperation, or an actual supernatural boost.
contrast: 仲間との絆: the bond itself, with less jokey trope language
ご都合主義: criticism that events work out too conveniently
example_ja_2: 友情パワーだけで勝つ結末には賛否が分かれた。
example_en_2: Viewers were divided over an ending won solely through the power of friendship.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume the phrase is always sincere praise. It can sarcastically criticize an unearned victory.

en: embarrassing past; personal history one wants buried
example_ja: 中学生のころのブログは、今では完全に黒歴史だ。
example_en: My middle-school blog is now an embarrassing chapter I would rather bury.
speaker_image: A speaker joking ruefully about an old creation, phase, or mistake they would prefer forgotten.
real_life_use: Now common beyond fandom. In serious historical writing, 黒い歴史 or 負の歴史 may be clearer than the slang sense.
usage_note_en: 黒歴史 labels a past episode the speaker treats as humiliating, regrettable, or disowned. It can range from playful self-mockery to concealed institutional history.
contrast: 恥ずかしい過去: plain description of an embarrassing past
消したい記憶: memory one wishes to erase, without the fixed slang label
example_ja_2: 昔の服装を黒歴史扱いするのはやめてよ。
example_en_2: Stop treating the way I used to dress as some shameful past.
misuse_note_en: English 'black history' has unrelated cultural meanings. Translate the intended regret or embarrassment rather than the characters literally.

en: so relatable; a familiar shared experience
example_ja: 締め切り前だけ部屋を掃除したくなるの、あるある。
example_en: Wanting to clean your room only when a deadline is near—so relatable.
speaker_image: A peer or online commenter recognizing a common experience shared by a group.
real_life_use: Very common in conversation, comedy, posts, and audience participation. Xあるある introduces a typical experience for group X.
usage_note_en: Repeated ある conveys 'that happens.' As a reaction, あるある enthusiastically confirms recognition; as a noun, it refers to the recurring pattern itself.
contrast: わかる: 'I get it/I relate,' responding from personal understanding
ありがち: common or predictable, often with mild criticism
example_ja_2: 学生あるあるを集めた動画を見た。
example_en_2: I watched a video collecting experiences every student knows.
misuse_note_en: There is no single fixed English noun equivalent. Translate it as 'relatable,' 'common experience,' or the specific recurring situation.

en: relatable comedy bit; joke built on a common experience
example_ja: コンビニ店員のあるあるネタで会場が笑った。
example_en: The audience laughed at a routine about situations every convenience-store clerk recognizes.
speaker_image: A comedian, creator, or viewer describing material based on familiar group experiences.
real_life_use: Common in comedy, short videos, articles, and social media. The group or setting is often placed before あるあるネタ.
usage_note_en: ネタ means material or a bit; あるあるネタ turns shared recognition into comedy or content. The point is familiarity more than a punch-line structure.
contrast: 内輪ネタ: joke understood mainly by insiders in a particular group
自虐ネタ: humor based on mocking oneself
example_ja_2: 在宅勤務のあるあるネタを四コマにした。
example_en_2: She turned familiar work-from-home situations into a four-panel comic.
misuse_note_en: Avoid the literal 'there-is-there-is material.' State who recognizes the situation and what kind of content it becomes.

example_ja: 重い話が続いたあとに、息抜きのギャグ回が入った。
example_en: After several heavy episodes, the series inserted a light comedy episode.
speaker_image: A fan or reviewer classifying an episode whose main purpose is comedy.
real_life_use: Common in episodic media discussion. It can be affectionate or dismissive depending on whether the speaker values the episode.
usage_note_en: 回 counts an installment or episode. A ギャグ回 shifts the usual tone toward jokes, even if it still contains plot information.
contrast: シリアス回: episode dominated by serious drama
日常回: episode centered on ordinary daily activity, not necessarily jokes
example_ja_2: 今回のギャグ回にも重要な伏線が隠れていた。
example_en_2: Even this week's comedy episode hid an important clue.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume a comedy episode is noncanonical or filler. Tone and plot relevance are separate questions.

example_ja: いつものコメディ調から一転して、今回はシリアス回だった。
example_en: This episode abandoned the usual comic tone for serious drama.
speaker_image: A fan or reviewer classifying an installment dominated by serious stakes or emotion.
real_life_use: Common in episodic media talk. シリアス is a Japanese loanword whose English equivalent is usually an adjective, so translate the whole phrase naturally.
usage_note_en: シリアス回 describes tone, not necessarily genre or quality. A series can alternate between comedic and serious episodes.
contrast: ギャグ回: comedy-focused episode
鬱展開: specifically bleak or emotionally punishing developments
example_ja_2: シリアス回の直後に総集編が放送された。
example_en_2: A recap aired immediately after the serious episode.
misuse_note_en: Avoid the unnatural English noun 'a seriousness episode.' Use 'serious episode,' 'dramatic installment,' or describe the tonal shift.

example_ja: 大きな事件が起きない日常系アニメをよく見る。
example_en: I often watch slice-of-life anime where no major incident occurs.
speaker_image: A fan, retailer, or critic classifying works centered on ordinary routines and relationships.
real_life_use: Standard in Japanese media discussion. Boundaries overlap with comedy, school stories, and iyashikei works.
usage_note_en: The suffix 系 means a type or family. 日常系 foregrounds everyday interaction and atmosphere rather than a strongly goal-driven plot.
contrast: 癒し系: soothing effect or type, which may overlap but is not identical
空気系: loosely connected character interaction and atmosphere, a narrower critical label
example_ja_2: 日常系に見えて、少しずつ謎が深まっていく作品だ。
example_en_2: It looks like a slice-of-life series, but its mystery gradually deepens.
misuse_note_en: Not every story set in daily life belongs to 日常系. The term usually implies that ordinary interaction is the main attraction.

example_ja: 家族の何気ない会話が続く、ほのぼのとした回だった。
example_en: It was a warm, gentle episode built around the family's everyday conversation.
speaker_image: A viewer or speaker responding to a calm, wholesome, pleasantly warm mood.
real_life_use: Common beyond fandom for stories, scenes, news, and atmospheres. ほのぼのする describes the warm feeling produced.
usage_note_en: ほのぼの suggests quiet warmth and emotional ease rather than excitement. The form ほのぼのとした commonly modifies a scene, story, or atmosphere.
contrast: のんびり: leisurely or unhurried
心温まる: explicitly heartwarming, often more emotionally pointed
example_ja_2: 子どもと犬が遊ぶ姿を見て、ほのぼのした。
example_en_2: Watching the child play with the dog gave me a warm feeling.
misuse_note_en: Do not force a single adjective such as 'heartwarming' every time. It can describe a gently peaceful tone with little emotional climax.

example_ja: 彼女は話し方が穏やかな癒し系キャラだ。
example_en: She is a soothing character with a gentle way of speaking.
speaker_image: A fan or acquaintance classifying a person, character, or work by the calming effect it has.
real_life_use: Used for celebrities, characters, music, spaces, and sometimes real people. Applying a type label to someone can flatten their personality.
usage_note_en: 癒し means emotional relief or comfort; 系 marks a type. 癒し系 emphasizes the recipient's calming impression rather than a literal healing ability.
contrast: 日常系: narrative genre centered on daily life
天然系: person perceived as naturally absent-minded or unconventional
example_ja_2: 疲れた日は癒し系の動画を見たくなる。
example_en_2: On tiring days, I want to watch calming videos.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it as a medical 'healing type.' In most media contexts, 'soothing,' 'comforting,' or 'feel-good' is natural.

example_ja: 努力と根性を信じる熱血な監督がチームを率いる。
example_en: A passionately intense coach who believes in effort and grit leads the team.
speaker_image: A fan or narrator describing an intensely passionate, idealistic, action-oriented person or style.
real_life_use: Used for teachers, coaches, characters, and story styles. It can praise commitment or criticize excessive intensity.
usage_note_en: Literally 'hot blood,' 熱血 evokes emotional fire, justice, perseverance, and loud encouragement. Compounds include 熱血漢 and 熱血教師.
contrast: 情熱的: passionate in a broad, neutral sense
暑苦しい: oppressively intense or overbearing, clearly negative
example_ja_2: 熱血指導が全員に合うとは限らない。
example_en_2: An intense coaching style does not suit everyone.
misuse_note_en: English 'hot-blooded' can suggest anger or sexuality. Translate the specific passion, idealism, or intensity intended by the context.

example_ja: 努力・友情・勝利を描く王道の少年漫画だ。
example_en: It is a classic shōnen manga built around effort, friendship, and victory.
speaker_image: A fan, critic, or creator praising or identifying a proven, central genre formula.
real_life_use: Common beyond fandom for strategies and methods. 王道 can mean the classic route, an orthodox approach, or the genre's main line.
usage_note_en: 王道 is usually positive: familiar elements executed in a satisfying way. It does not necessarily mean stale or unoriginal.
contrast: 定番: standard favorite or staple
邪道: unorthodox or improper route, often used playfully as the opposite
example_ja_2: 奇抜さより王道を丁寧に描いた作品だ。
example_en_2: The work carefully executes a classic formula instead of chasing novelty.
misuse_note_en: Avoid the literal 'royal road' unless explaining the Japanese term. Also do not equate 王道 automatically with cliché; evaluation depends on execution.

example_ja: アニメを見たあとで原作の小説を読んだ。
example_en: After watching the anime, I read the original novel.
speaker_image: A viewer, publisher, or creator identifying the work on which an adaptation is based.
real_life_use: Standard in publishing and media discussion. The 原作 may be a manga, novel, game, or other prior work.
usage_note_en: 原作 is the source work itself, not merely an earlier version. Credits may separately name 原案 for the underlying concept and original ideas.
contrast: 原案: original concept or story outline
オリジナル作品: work not adapted from existing source material
example_ja_2: 映画版では原作の結末が変更されている。
example_en_2: The film adaptation changes the ending of the source material.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 原作 as 'original story' when discussing a source manga or game; 'source material' is often clearer.

en: anime adaptation; to be adapted into anime
example_ja: 連載中の漫画が来年アニメ化される。
example_en: The manga currently being serialized will receive an anime adaptation next year.
speaker_image: A publisher, fan, or journalist discussing adaptation into animated form.
real_life_use: Standard industry and fan vocabulary. The source is marked with が in the passive pattern Xがアニメ化される.
usage_note_en: The suffix 化 means turning something into a form or state. アニメ化 refers to the process or result of adapting source material as animation.
contrast: 実写化: adaptation into live-action film or television
映像化: broader screen adaptation, whether animated or live action
example_ja_2: アニメ化を機に原作の売り上げが伸びた。
example_en_2: Sales of the source material rose after the anime adaptation.
misuse_note_en: Do not call every animated version a remake. アニメ化 specifically describes adaptation into animation, often for the first time.

en: live-action adaptation; to adapt as live action
example_ja: その漫画は映画として実写化された。
example_en: The manga was adapted into a live-action film.
speaker_image: A fan, producer, or journalist discussing a version performed by human actors.
real_life_use: Standard media vocabulary. 映画化 or ドラマ化 may additionally specify the release format.
usage_note_en: 実写 means live-action photography as opposed to animation. 実写化 can adapt manga, anime, novels, or games into film, television, or web productions.
contrast: アニメ化: adaptation into animation
映画化: film adaptation, which may be live action or animated
example_ja_2: 実写化では衣装の再現が難しそうだ。
example_en_2: Recreating the costumes may be difficult in live action.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it as 'made real.' The term describes the production medium, not whether the story becomes realistic.

example_ja: 戦闘シーンは動きも表情も作画が細かい。
example_en: The battle scene has detailed animation in both movement and facial expression.
speaker_image: An animator, critic, or fan discussing the drawn visual execution of animation.
real_life_use: Standard within animation production and common in fandom. Fans also use 作画 evaluatively, but the word itself does not mean 'quality.'
usage_note_en: 作画 literally refers to making the drawings. In anime discussion it can cover character drawings and animated movement; 作画がいい supplies the positive judgment.
contrast: 絵柄: visual drawing style
演出: direction and presentation of a scene
example_ja_2: 話数ごとに作画監督がクレジットされている。
example_en_2: An animation director is credited for each episode.
misuse_note_en: Do not define 作画 as 'animation quality' alone. Bad, good, limited, and detailed 作画 are all possible; the evaluation comes from context.

example_ja: 同じ声優が少年役と老人役を演じ分けている。
example_en: The same voice actor performs both the boy and the old man with distinct voices.
speaker_image: A viewer or industry worker referring to a performer who acts through voice.
real_life_use: Standard professional term for performers in animation, games, dubbing, narration, and audio drama. It is gender-neutral.
usage_note_en: 声優 is a specialized acting profession, not simply anyone who supplies a voice. Common verbs include 演じる, 担当する, and 声を当てる.
contrast: 俳優: actor, often associated with live-action or stage performance
ナレーター: performer specializing in narration
example_ja_2: 主人公の声優は海外版の吹き替えにも参加した。
example_en_2: The protagonist's voice actor also took part in dubbing the overseas version.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 女性声優 as 'voice actress' automatically unless the context prefers gendered English; 'voice actor' is broadly standard.

example_ja: 映画の主題歌を主演俳優が歌っている。
example_en: The film's lead actor sings its theme song.
speaker_image: A viewer, musician, or promoter discussing a song associated centrally with a work.
real_life_use: Standard for films, dramas, anime, and programs. In anime, either an opening or ending may be promoted as the 主題歌.
usage_note_en: 主題歌 is the work's designated theme song. It need not literally state the story's theme, and some works have multiple theme songs.
contrast: オープニング曲: song used in the opening sequence
挿入歌: song inserted within an episode or scene
example_ja_2: 主題歌の歌詞が物語の結末と重なる。
example_en_2: The theme song's lyrics echo the story's ending.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 主題歌 always means the opening. Check credits or context to see whether it is an opening, ending, or film theme.

example_ja: 静かなエンディング曲が余韻を残した。
example_en: The quiet ending theme let the episode's mood linger.
speaker_image: A viewer or production member referring to music used over the ending sequence or credits.
real_life_use: Common for anime and television. The abbreviation ED is also used in fandom and production listings.
usage_note_en: エンディング曲 identifies placement at the end, not a particular musical style. A series may change the song by season or episode.
contrast: オープニング曲: opening theme
挿入歌: song heard within the main story
example_ja_2: 最終回だけエンディング曲の二番が流れた。
example_en_2: Only the finale used the second verse of the ending theme.
misuse_note_en: Do not confuse the ending song with the background score that happens to play near the end of a scene.

example_ja: 最終回では十年後の登場人物たちが描かれた。
example_en: The finale showed the characters ten years later.
speaker_image: A viewer, broadcaster, or critic referring to the last installment of a series or season.
real_life_use: Standard for television, web series, radio, and serialized programs. Context determines whether it is the end of a season or the entire work.
usage_note_en: 回 counts episodes; 最終回 is the last scheduled installment of the relevant run. A later sequel can still follow.
contrast: 最終話: final story chapter or episode, often in narrative works
完結編: concluding installment or arc designed to finish the whole work
example_ja_2: 来週の最終回は放送時間が三十分延長される。
example_en_2: Next week's finale will have an extra thirty minutes.
misuse_note_en: Do not infer that the franchise has permanently ended. 最終回 may close only the current season or broadcast run.

example_ja: 次回予告で新しい敵の姿が映った。
example_en: A new enemy appeared in the preview for the next episode.
speaker_image: A viewer or broadcaster referring to the short preview following an episode.
real_life_use: Standard in television and episodic media. 予告 alone may mean a trailer or advance notice more broadly.
usage_note_en: 次回 means the next installment, and 予告 announces it in advance. Previews may use narration, clips, title cards, or deliberately comic material.
contrast: 予告編: trailer, especially for a film or work as a whole
番宣: promotional content for a program
example_ja_2: 次回予告を見ずに、そのまま再生を止めた。
example_en_2: I stopped playback without watching the next-episode preview.
misuse_note_en: Do not call a full-series trailer 次回予告. The word points specifically to the next installment.

example_ja: 第一話の何気ない会話が重要な伏線になっている。
example_en: A casual conversation in episode one becomes important foreshadowing.
speaker_image: A writer, critic, or viewer identifying an earlier detail that prepares for a later revelation.
real_life_use: Standard in narrative discussion. Casual fans sometimes call any unexplained detail 伏線, though not every mystery is deliberate foreshadowing.
usage_note_en: A 伏線 is planted in advance so a later event feels prepared or meaningful. It can be dialogue, imagery, behavior, or background information.
contrast: ヒント: clue or hint that may directly aid inference
ミスリード: detail designed to steer the audience toward a wrong conclusion
example_ja_2: 作者は結末につながる伏線を各章に張っていた。
example_en_2: The author planted clues leading to the ending in every chapter.
misuse_note_en: Do not label every unresolved question a 伏線. It may be atmosphere, world-building, a loose end, or simply an error.

en: payoff or resolution of earlier setup
example_ja: 第一話の台詞が最終回で伏線回収された。
example_en: A line from the first episode paid off in the finale.
speaker_image: A fan or critic recognizing how a later reveal gives meaning to an earlier detail.
real_life_use: Very common in reviews and online discussion. The 回収 metaphor treats planted setup as something collected later.
usage_note_en: 伏線回収 is the payoff, explanation, or fulfillment of foreshadowing. Japanese allows 伏線を回収する and 伏線が回収される.
contrast: 謎解き: solving a mystery
どんでん返し: reversal that changes the audience's understanding
example_ja_2: 未回収の伏線がいくつか残っている。
example_en_2: Several planted threads remain unresolved.
misuse_note_en: English 'collect the foreshadowing' is unnatural. Use 'pay off,' 'resolve,' or 'tie up' according to the sentence.

example_ja: 脚本と演出がかみ合った神回だった。
example_en: It was an exceptional episode in which the writing and direction worked perfectly together.
speaker_image: An enthusiastic fan singling out one episode for unusually high praise.
real_life_use: Common in posts, comments, and casual reviews. It is subjective hyperbole rather than an industry rating.
usage_note_en: 神 works as a slang intensifier meaning outstanding. 回 refers to one installment, so 神回 praises a particular episode rather than the series as a whole.
contrast: 神アニメ: praise for an anime as a whole
当たり回: an especially enjoyable episode, often less emphatic
example_ja_2: ファンの間では第八話が神回と呼ばれている。
example_en_2: Fans often call episode eight the series' standout episode.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 神 literally in ordinary English or present 神回 as an objective label.

example_ja: 放送前から覇権アニメ候補として注目されていた。
example_en: Even before airing, it was seen as a contender to dominate the anime season.
speaker_image: A fan or commentator arguing that one title leads a season in attention, popularity, sales, or influence.
real_life_use: Common but contested fandom shorthand. Different speakers use different evidence, so claims should state the metric.
usage_note_en: 覇権 literally concerns supremacy. 覇権アニメ frames seasonal anime as a competition, but there is no single official criterion for winning.
contrast: 人気作: popular work without claiming seasonal dominance
話題作: much-discussed or anticipated work
example_ja_2: 配信再生数だけで覇権アニメを決めるのは難しい。
example_en_2: It is hard to name a season's dominant anime from streaming views alone.
misuse_note_en: Do not define it simply as 'the most popular anime.' Sales, online buzz, streaming, and personal preference are often mixed together.

example_ja: 配信の視聴者から質問を募集した。
example_en: The stream invited questions from viewers.
speaker_image: A broadcaster, researcher, or commentator referring to people who watch a program or stream.
real_life_use: Standard across television, video, live streams, and media measurement. It is more formal than casual 見ている人.
usage_note_en: 視聴 combines seeing and listening, and 者 marks a person. The term treats people in their role as audience members.
contrast: 観客: audience physically attending a performance or event
読者: reader of written material
example_ja_2: 視聴者の半数以上がスマートフォンで番組を見ていた。
example_en_2: More than half of the viewers watched the program on a smartphone.
misuse_note_en: Do not use 視聴者 for readers or game players unless they are specifically watching video content.

example_ja: 考察勢が背景の記号から黒幕を予想している。
example_en: Theory-crafting fans are using symbols in the background to predict the mastermind.
speaker_image: A fan informally grouping people who closely analyze clues and build theories.
real_life_use: Common online. The suffix 勢 labels a loosely defined camp or cohort, not an official organization.
usage_note_en: 考察 in fandom means evidence-based interpretation or theorizing. 考察勢 are the participants known for that activity.
contrast: 考察班: playful label for an analysis 'team'
感想勢: people focused more on reactions and impressions than theories
example_ja_2: 考察勢の動画を見てから、第一話を見直した。
example_en_2: After watching a fan theory video, I rewatched the first episode.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 勢 literally as 'forces.' Use 'fans,' 'crowd,' or 'people who...' according to tone.

example_ja: 週末に全十二話を一気見した。
example_en: I binge-watched all twelve episodes over the weekend.
speaker_image: A viewer describing watching many installments consecutively or in a short period.
real_life_use: Common across television, anime, and online video. 一気に見る is the transparent full phrase.
usage_note_en: 一気 means in one burst. 一気見 does not require literally one uninterrupted sitting; the emphasis is rapid consecutive viewing.
contrast: 見返す: watch again
流し見: watch with partial attention while doing something else
example_ja_2: 一気見すると細かい伏線に気づきやすい。
example_en_2: Binge-watching makes the small pieces of foreshadowing easier to notice.
misuse_note_en: Do not use the verb without する in formal grammar: 一気見した is the common verbal pattern.

example_ja: この作品は定額プランで見放題になっている。
example_en: This title is included with the flat-rate streaming plan.
speaker_image: A service, customer, or fan discussing content available without per-title charges.
real_life_use: Common in streaming advertisements and plan descriptions. Availability may still depend on subscription, region, and period.
usage_note_en: The 〜放題 pattern means doing as much as desired. 見放題 usually means unlimited viewing within a plan, not that access is free.
contrast: レンタル: time-limited access purchased per title
無料配信: distributed without a viewing charge
example_ja_2: 見放題の対象から来月外れるらしい。
example_en_2: Apparently it will leave the subscription catalog next month.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 見放題 as 'free to watch' unless no payment is required. A paid subscription can provide 見放題.

example_ja: 俳優本人の声を聞きたいので字幕版を選んだ。
example_en: I chose the subtitled version because I wanted to hear the actors' original voices.
speaker_image: A viewer, cinema, or platform distinguishing a version with translated subtitles.
real_life_use: Standard for foreign films and programs in Japan. The subtitle language is normally understood from the market but can be specified.
usage_note_en: 版 means version or edition. 字幕版 contrasts with a version whose spoken dialogue has been replaced by dubbing.
contrast: 吹き替え版: dubbed version
字幕付き: content with subtitles, including same-language accessibility captions
example_ja_2: 字幕版と吹き替え版では上映時間が違う。
example_en_2: The subtitled and dubbed versions have different screening times.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 字幕版 always means accessibility captions. In release listings, it usually means translated subtitles with the original audio.

example_ja: 子どもと一緒なので日本語の吹き替え版を見た。
example_en: Because I was watching with children, I chose the Japanese dub.
speaker_image: A viewer, cinema, or platform identifying a version with replaced spoken dialogue.
real_life_use: Standard for films, television, and animation. The target language can be stated as 日本語吹き替え版.
usage_note_en: 吹き替え replaces original spoken voices with performances in another language. It is distinct from voice-over narration.
contrast: 字幕版: original audio with translated subtitles
ボイスオーバー: another voice layered over audible original speech
example_ja_2: 吹き替え版では台詞が口の動きに合わせて調整されている。
example_en_2: In the dubbed version, the dialogue is adjusted to match the mouth movements.
misuse_note_en: Do not call an anime's original Japanese voice track a Japanese 吹き替え. Dubbing replaces an earlier-language performance.

example_ja: まだ見ていない人がいるから、結末のネタバレはやめよう。
example_en: Some people have not seen it yet, so let's not spoil the ending.
speaker_image: A viewer warning about or revealing information that removes a story surprise.
real_life_use: Very common. ネタバレあり warns that spoilers follow; ネタバレする means to spoil a plot point.
usage_note_en: ネタ refers here to story content, and ばれ comes from exposure or discovery. The word can name the information, the act, or a warning category.
contrast: あらすじ: plot summary, which may avoid major reveals
匂わせ: indirect hinting that suggests information without stating it openly
example_ja_2: レビューの冒頭に『ネタバレあり』と書いておいた。
example_en_2: I put a spoiler warning at the start of the review.
misuse_note_en: A title, premise, or officially advertised fact is not automatically a spoiler. Audience expectations and timing matter.

example_ja: 考察班が予告映像を一コマずつ確認している。
example_en: The fan-analysis crowd is checking the trailer frame by frame.
speaker_image: A fan playfully treating people who develop theories as an organized investigation team.
real_life_use: Common online, though the 'team' is often imaginary or loosely self-appointed rather than an actual group.
usage_note_en: 班 normally means a small team. In fandom, 考察班 humorously labels the people who collect clues and test interpretations.
contrast: 考察勢: the broader cohort of theory-focused fans
検証班: people checking whether a claim or detail is accurate
example_ja_2: この暗号は考察班に任せよう。
example_en_2: Let's leave this code to the fandom detectives.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 考察班 is an official production unit. Translate the playful fan role rather than a literal workplace team.

example_ja: 放送日は公式サイトで確認してください。
example_en: Check the broadcast date on the official website.
speaker_image: A fan, company, or customer distinguishing authorized information from unofficial material.
real_life_use: Extremely common. 公式 can modify サイト, アカウント, 発表, and other nouns, or stand alone for the rights holder's public channel.
usage_note_en: 公式 literally means an official form or formula, but media usage commonly means authorized by the publisher, studio, creator, or other relevant organization.
contrast: 非公式: unofficial
公認: recognized or approved by an authority, not necessarily produced by it
example_ja_2: その画像は公式が公開したものではない。
example_en_2: That image was not released by the official account.
misuse_note_en: Do not equate 公式 with objectively true. An official source is authoritative about its own decisions, but translations and announcements can still contain errors.

kana: せっていしりょうしゅう
example_ja: 設定資料集には衣装の背面図も載っている。
example_en: The production reference book includes rear views of the costumes.
speaker_image: A creator, collector, or fan referring to a book of visual and written production settings.
real_life_use: Common for animation, games, and films. Content may include model sheets, props, locations, timelines, and creator notes.
usage_note_en: 設定資料 are reference materials defining a work; 集 means a collection. The book may be official, but the term itself does not guarantee publisher authorization.
contrast: 画集: art book focused on finished illustrations
公式ガイドブック: authorized guide with summaries and reference information
example_ja_2: 図書館で昔のアニメの設定資料集を見つけた。
example_en_2: I found a production-design reference book for an old anime at the library.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 設定資料集 as 'official art book.' It may focus on technical reference drawings, and official status must be confirmed separately.

en: fictional world and its underlying outlook; setting
example_ja: 科学と魔法が共存する世界観が魅力だ。
example_en: The work's world, where science and magic coexist, is compelling.
speaker_image: A creator, critic, or fan discussing the coherent feel, assumptions, and values of a fictional world.
real_life_use: Also used philosophically for a person's worldview. In media talk, it often covers more than physical setting.
usage_note_en: 世界観 literally means a view of the world. Japanese media usage can include setting, atmosphere, rules, history, and values; English 'worldbuilding' fits only some contexts.
contrast: 設定: specific premise, rule, or assigned detail
舞台: the place and time where events occur
example_ja_2: 音楽が作品の独特な世界観を支えている。
example_en_2: The music supports the work's distinctive atmosphere and worldview.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 世界観 as 'worldbuilding,' which describes a creative process. Sometimes 'world,' 'aesthetic,' 'setting,' or 'worldview' is better.

example_ja: 制服のキャラデザは原案よりシンプルになった。
example_en: The uniform designs were simplified from the original concepts.
speaker_image: A fan or production worker using shorthand for a character's visual design.
real_life_use: Common abbreviation of キャラクターデザイン in credits and fandom. Formal credits may use the full expression.
usage_note_en: キャラデザ can refer to the design work or resulting designs: silhouette, clothing, colors, facial features, and model choices.
contrast: キャラクター原案: initial character concept designs
作画: the drawing and animation of characters in actual footage
example_ja_2: キャラデザ担当のインタビューを読んだ。
example_en_2: I read an interview with the character designer.
misuse_note_en: Do not use キャラデザ as a synonym for animation quality. A design can remain strong even when individual drawings vary.

example_ja: 物語が完結する前に連載が打ち切りになった。
example_en: The serialization was canceled before the story could reach its conclusion.
speaker_image: A publisher, fan, or journalist discussing a work ended earlier than planned.
real_life_use: Used for manga, television, projects, and services. It does not state the cause unless one is added.
usage_note_en: 打ち切る means to stop something at a cutoff point. A 打ち切り may result from sales, scheduling, production trouble, or other decisions.
contrast: 完結: narrative reaches its conclusion
休載: publication pauses rather than ends
example_ja_2: 視聴率だけが打ち切りの理由とは限らない。
example_en_2: Ratings are not necessarily the only reason a program is canceled.
misuse_note_en: Do not assert that low popularity caused a 打ち切り without evidence. The word describes the early end, not its verified reason.

example_ja: 十年間続いた漫画が今月完結した。
example_en: The manga concluded this month after a ten-year run.
speaker_image: A creator, publisher, or reader stating that a narrative has reached its intended end.
real_life_use: Common for stories, series, arguments, and multi-part works. 完結編 names the concluding installment.
usage_note_en: 完結 emphasizes closure as a complete whole. It differs from merely stopping publication or broadcasting.
contrast: 終了: ends or stops, without promising narrative resolution
打ち切り: is cut short before the expected completion
example_ja_2: 物語は映画三部作で完結する予定だ。
example_en_2: The story is scheduled to conclude with a trilogy of films.
misuse_note_en: Do not use 'completed' to imply every mystery was resolved; 完結 states that the work ended as a whole, not that every reader found it satisfying.

example_ja: その漫画は月刊誌で連載されている。
example_en: The manga is serialized in a monthly magazine.
speaker_image: A publisher, creator, or reader discussing regular installment publication.
real_life_use: Standard for manga, novels, essays, and web content. The publication venue is commonly marked with で.
usage_note_en: 連載 means a work appears in successive installments. It can be ongoing, finished, paused, or later collected into volumes.
contrast: 掲載: an item is printed or posted, whether once or repeatedly
単行本化: installments are collected and published as a book
example_ja_2: ウェブで連載中の小説が書籍化された。
example_en_2: The novel currently serialized online was published as a book.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 連載中 simply as 'being written.' It specifically describes ongoing publication in installments.

example_ja: 作者の体調不良により、今週は休載となった。
example_en: This week's installment was paused because of the author's poor health.
speaker_image: A publisher, creator, or reader discussing a temporary break in serialized publication.
real_life_use: Standard. A single skipped issue and a long hiatus can both be described with 休載, so duration requires context.
usage_note_en: 休載 combines rest with publication. It normally implies that a serialized work is not appearing as scheduled, without declaring it canceled.
contrast: 打ち切り: publication ends prematurely
連載終了: serialization has ended, whether planned or not
example_ja_2: 三か月の休載を経て、連載が再開した。
example_en_2: The series resumed after a three-month hiatus.
misuse_note_en: Do not report a work as canceled merely because it is 休載. Check whether a return date or indefinite hiatus has been announced.

example_ja: 雑誌で読んだ話が単行本に収録された。
example_en: The chapter I read in the magazine was collected in a book volume.
speaker_image: A publisher, bookseller, or reader distinguishing a book-format volume from magazine installments.
real_life_use: Common for manga and other books. In manga contexts, English 'collected volume' or simply 'volume' is usually natural.
usage_note_en: A 単行本 is a separately published book, often collecting material first serialized elsewhere. It is not inherently a one-volume complete work.
contrast: 雑誌: periodical carrying multiple works or installments
文庫本: small-format paperback edition
example_ja_2: 単行本には描き下ろしの短編が追加されている。
example_en_2: The collected volume adds a newly drawn short story.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 単行本 as 'single-volume book.' A manga series can have dozens of 単行本 volumes.

example_ja: 好きな漫画の新刊が来週発売される。
example_en: The latest volume of my favorite manga comes out next week.
speaker_image: A bookseller, publisher, or reader referring to a newly released book.
real_life_use: Common in bookstores and publishing. Context decides whether it means any new title or the newest volume in a series.
usage_note_en: 新刊 literally means a newly published book. Xの新刊 often means an author's or series' latest release.
contrast: 既刊: volumes or titles already published
新作: new creative work, not necessarily a book
example_ja_2: 書店の新刊コーナーで面白そうな小説を見つけた。
example_en_2: I found an interesting-looking novel in the bookstore's new-release section.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 新刊 always means volume one or a brand-new series. It may be the next volume of a long-running work.

en: published volumes to date; existing backlist
example_ja: 休みに入る前に既刊を全巻そろえた。
example_en: Before the holiday, I bought every volume published so far.
speaker_image: A publisher, retailer, or reader referring collectively to books already released.
real_life_use: Common in series listings and publishing. The current number is often stated as 既刊十二巻.
usage_note_en: 既 means already, so 既刊 contrasts released books with forthcoming ones. It may refer to one author's backlist or a series' existing volumes.
contrast: 新刊: newly published or latest book
未刊: not yet published
example_ja_2: このシリーズは既刊八巻で、九巻は秋に出る。
example_en_2: The series has eight published volumes, and volume nine arrives in autumn.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 既刊 as 'old books.' Recently released volumes are still 既刊 once published.

en: buying a book for its cover
example_ja: 書店で表紙にひかれて表紙買いした。
example_en: The cover caught my eye at the bookstore, so I bought the book on that basis.
speaker_image: A reader admitting that the cover design motivated a purchase before the content did.
real_life_use: Common casual term for books and manga. It does not necessarily mean the buyer regrets the choice or knew nothing else.
usage_note_en: The productive pattern X買い means buying because of X. 表紙買い makes cover art, typography, or design the deciding signal.
contrast: 作者買い: purchase based on the author
ジャケ買い: buy music or other media for its jacket or package art
example_ja_2: 表紙買いだったけど、内容も好みに合った。
example_en_2: I bought it for the cover, but the story suited my tastes too.
misuse_note_en: Avoid the literal 'cover buying.' In English, explain that the cover drove the purchase.

en: buying a work because of its author
example_ja: あの作家の小説は内容を確認せずに作者買いする。
example_en: I buy that writer's novels on the strength of the author's name alone.
speaker_image: A loyal reader explaining that trust in a creator drives purchases.
real_life_use: Common for books and manga. Similar compounds can use 監督, 声優, or レーベル as the purchase reason.
usage_note_en: 作者買い means choosing a new title because its author made it, often without needing reviews or a detailed synopsis.
contrast: 表紙買い: purchase driven by cover design
指名買い: deliberately buy a specified brand, creator, or product
example_ja_2: 作者買いした新刊が、いつもの作風と全く違って驚いた。
example_en_2: I bought the new book because of the author and was surprised by how different it was from their usual style.
misuse_note_en: The term describes purchase motivation, not ownership of the author. Translate the reason naturally.

example_ja: 最終話の収録後にスタッフが打ち上げを開いた。
example_en: The staff held a wrap party after recording the final episode.
speaker_image: A production member or organizer celebrating completion of a project, event, or performance.
real_life_use: Common across film, television, theater, events, and projects. 打ち上げ also means launching something, including fireworks or a rocket.
usage_note_en: In the party sense, 打ち上げ is a gathering after work concludes or reaches a milestone. The object and verb distinguish it from a physical launch.
contrast: 飲み会: drinking party without a completion requirement
打ち入り: kickoff gathering before a major project or production
example_ja_2: 花火の打ち上げは午後八時から始まる。
example_en_2: The fireworks launch begins at eight in the evening.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 打ち上げ as 'wrap party.' Rockets, fireworks, and project celebrations use the same noun in different senses.

en: editor assigned to a creator; editor in charge
example_ja: 漫画家は新しい担当編集と次回作を相談した。
example_en: The manga artist discussed the next project with the newly assigned editor.
speaker_image: A creator or publisher referring to the editor responsible for a particular author or work.
real_life_use: Standard publishing vocabulary. In conversation, 担当 alone may mean the assigned editor when the context is clear.
usage_note_en: 担当 means being in charge, and 編集 identifies the editorial role. The editor may coordinate deadlines, give story feedback, and connect the creator with the publisher.
contrast: 編集長: editor in chief overseeing an editorial department or publication
担当者: person in charge in any field
example_ja_2: 担当編集からネームの修正案が届いた。
example_en_2: The assigned editor sent suggestions for revising the manga storyboard.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 担当編集 is the sole creative author or merely a proofreader. Responsibilities vary by publisher and work.

example_ja: 新人賞を取った読み切りが雑誌に掲載された。
example_en: The award-winning one-shot was published in the magazine.
speaker_image: A publisher, creator, or reader discussing a story designed to be complete in one installment.
real_life_use: Standard in manga and fiction publishing. A successful 読み切り can later be expanded into a series.
usage_note_en: As a noun, 読み切り is a complete standalone piece. It derives from 読み切る, to read through or finish reading, but the publishing term has a fixed sense.
contrast: 連載: serialization across multiple installments
短編: short work, which may be published alone or within a collection
example_ja_2: 連載版では読み切りの設定が一部変更された。
example_en_2: The serialized version changed some of the one-shot's premises.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it as 'reading to the end.' Distinguish the noun label 読み切り from the verb 読み切る.

example_ja: 番外編では脇役たちの休日が描かれる。
example_en: The side story follows the supporting characters on their day off.
speaker_image: A publisher, creator, or fan identifying an installment outside the main narrative line.
real_life_use: Common in manga, anime, novels, and programs. It may be canonical, comedic, retrospective, or promotional.
usage_note_en: 番外 means outside the regular numbering or main sequence. 番外編 adds material beside the central story rather than necessarily continuing it.
contrast: 外伝: spin-off or supplementary tale, often larger and more independent
特別編: special installment created for a particular occasion or format
example_ja_2: 単行本の巻末に番外編が収録されている。
example_en_2: A bonus story is included at the end of the collected volume.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 番外編 is noncanonical or disposable filler. Its relationship to continuity depends on the work.

example_ja: 今週はこれまでの戦いを振り返る総集編だった。
example_en: This week's episode was a recap of the battles so far.
speaker_image: A broadcaster, publisher, or viewer referring to material compiled from earlier installments.
real_life_use: Used for recap episodes, compilation films, and collected print editions. The medium determines the natural English term.
usage_note_en: 総集編 gathers selected prior content into one edition. It may add narration or new footage, but compilation remains the main structure.
contrast: 再放送: rebroadcast of an earlier episode as-is
ダイジェスト: condensed highlights or summary
example_ja_2: 劇場版はテレビシリーズ前半の総集編になっている。
example_en_2: The theatrical film compiles the first half of the television series.
misuse_note_en: Do not call every 総集編 a 'recap episode.' In film or print, 'compilation film' or 'collected edition' may fit better.

example_ja: 同じ世界を舞台にした新シリーズが始まる。
example_en: A new series set in the same world is beginning.
speaker_image: A publisher, producer, or fan discussing the launch of another series or branded run.
real_life_use: Common and broad. It may be a sequel, reboot, new season, spin-off, or unrelated series from the same creator.
usage_note_en: シリーズ is flexible in Japanese. 新シリーズ says a new series begins but does not define its continuity or production format.
contrast: 新シーズン: new season of an existing series
続編: sequel continuing an earlier work
example_ja_2: 新シリーズは主人公も時代も一新される。
example_en_2: The new series changes both the protagonist and the time period.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 新シリーズ automatically as 'new season.' Confirm whether it is a sequel, reboot, spin-off, or separate line.

en: favorite person, character, team, or work one supports
example_ja: この作品では無口な脇役が私の推しだ。
example_en: My favorite in this series is the quiet supporting character.
speaker_image: A fan naming the person, character, group, or work they feel especially attached to and support.
real_life_use: Now widely recognized beyond dedicated fandom. The object may be real or fictional and does not necessarily imply romantic attraction.
usage_note_en: 推し derives from 推す, to recommend or back. As a noun it means the target a fan actively favors, often with an element of support beyond simple liking.
contrast: お気に入り: a favorite, with less fandom or support implication
担当: one's favored idol or member in some specific fandom traditions
example_ja_2: 推しが新曲のセンターに選ばれた。
example_en_2: My favorite member was chosen as the center for the new song.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 推し as 'crush.' Fans can have multiple 推し and may support them for performance, design, personality, or story role.

en: fan activities supporting and enjoying one's favorite
example_ja: 週末は友達と推し活でコラボカフェに行く。
example_en: This weekend, I'm going to a collaboration café with friends as part of our fan activities.
speaker_image: A fan positively framing the time, purchases, visits, and creative activities centered on a favorite.
real_life_use: Common in marketing and everyday fan talk. Activities can include attending events, buying goods, posting, traveling, or simply watching.
usage_note_en: 推し活 combines 推し with 活動. It packages many forms of support and enjoyment as an ongoing lifestyle activity.
contrast: オタ活: fan or otaku activities more broadly
ファン活動: neutral general term for fan activity
example_ja_2: 無理のない予算で推し活を続けたい。
example_en_2: I want to keep supporting my favorite without exceeding my budget.
misuse_note_en: Do not define 推し活 only as buying merchandise. Noncommercial participation and personal enjoyment also count.

en: fall deep into a fandom or hobby
example_ja: 一話だけ見るつもりが、すっかり作品の沼にはまった。
example_en: I meant to watch one episode and ended up completely absorbed in the series.
speaker_image: A fan humorously describing an interest that has become deep, consuming, and hard to leave.
real_life_use: Common for hobbies, genres, performers, tools, and collecting. The metaphor can be positive despite 沼 literally being a swamp.
usage_note_en: The image is of stepping into a deep swamp and being unable to get out. X沼 means the absorbing world surrounding X.
contrast: 夢中になる: become engrossed, neutral and broadly usable
ハマる: get hooked on something, without the same depth metaphor
example_ja_2: 友達に勧められて、カメラ沼にはまった。
example_en_2: A friend's recommendation sent me deep into the camera hobby.
misuse_note_en: Avoid the literal English 'fall into a swamp' unless explaining the metaphor. The phrase usually expresses enthusiastic absorption, not actual distress.

en: enthusiastically recruit someone into a fandom; recommend
example_ja: 友達にこの漫画を布教して、全巻貸した。
example_en: I tried to get my friend into the manga and lent them every volume.
speaker_image: An enthusiastic fan joking that recommending a beloved work resembles missionary activity.
real_life_use: Common online among fans. Outside slang, 布教 literally concerns spreading a religion, so context and audience matter.
usage_note_en: Fandom 布教する means actively introducing and promoting a work, performer, or hobby in hopes that others become fans.
contrast: 勧める: recommend, neutral and broadly appropriate
宣伝する: advertise or publicize, often to a wider audience
example_ja_2: 初心者向けの曲をまとめて、バンドを布教している。
example_en_2: I made a beginner-friendly playlist to introduce people to the band.
misuse_note_en: Do not use the fandom joke in serious religious contexts, and do not translate it as literal evangelism when a simple recommendation is meant.

en: visiting real locations associated with a work
example_ja: アニメの舞台になった町を聖地巡礼した。
example_en: I visited the town that served as the anime's setting.
speaker_image: A fan traveling to real sites shown in or connected with a favorite work.
real_life_use: Widely used in tourism promotion as well as fandom. The original meaning is religious pilgrimage to sacred places and remains active.
usage_note_en: Fandom metaphorically treats filming or model locations as 聖地, sacred sites. Visits may include photography, local shops, and comparison with scenes.
