contrast: ロケ地巡り: visiting filming locations, without the sacred-site fandom metaphor
巡礼: pilgrimage or a circuit of significant sites more broadly
example_ja_2: 聖地巡礼では住民の迷惑にならないように撮影した。
example_en_2: While visiting the anime locations, we took photos without disturbing residents.
misuse_note_en: Respect access rules and local residents. A work's association with a place does not grant fans permission to enter private property.

example_ja: 好きな作品の二次創作イラストを投稿した。
example_en: I posted fan art based on a series I like.
speaker_image: A fan creator or rights holder discussing new work based on existing characters, settings, or stories.
real_life_use: Common for fan art, fan fiction, comics, music, video, and games. Rules and tolerated uses differ by rights holder and platform.
usage_note_en: 二次創作 literally means secondary creation derived from an earlier work. It is broader than fan fiction and does not itself state commercial status or legality.
contrast: 一次創作: original creation not derived from another work
公式作品: work created or authorized by the rights holder
example_ja_2: 公式の二次創作ガイドラインを読んでから公開した。
example_en_2: I read the official derivative-work guidelines before publishing it.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume all 二次創作 is automatically licensed, noncommercial, or legally permitted. Check the relevant rights and guidelines.

example_ja: イベントで創作漫画の同人誌を頒布した。
example_en: I distributed a self-published original comic at the event.
speaker_image: A creator, buyer, or event participant discussing independently produced publications.
real_life_use: Common in fan and independent creative communities. A 同人誌 may be derivative or completely original, and may contain any rating.
usage_note_en: 同人誌 is a publication made by an individual or circle outside mainstream commercial publishing. Manga, fiction, essays, criticism, and research all occur.
contrast: 商業誌: commercially published magazine or book
二次創作: derivative creation in any medium, not necessarily a printed dōjinshi
example_ja_2: 評論系の同人誌を専門に扱う店もある。
example_en_2: Some shops specialize in independently published criticism and research.
misuse_note_en: Do not define 同人誌 as pornographic fan comics. It can be all-ages, original, academic, or prose, and the term refers to publication context.

example_ja: イベントでゲームの主人公をコスプレした。
example_en: I cosplayed as the game's protagonist at the event.
speaker_image: A participant dressing and often posing as a character or themed figure.
real_life_use: Widely understood. Japanese commonly uses Xのコスプレをする or Xをコスプレする, though the former is clearer.
usage_note_en: コスプレ is shortened from costume play. It includes making or wearing costumes, makeup, photography, and performance to varying degrees.
contrast: 仮装: dressing up or wearing a disguise more broadly
着ぐるみ: full-body character suit or mascot costume
example_ja_2: 衣装は自作だが、コスプレ会場でしか着ない。
example_en_2: I made the costume myself, but I only wear it at cosplay venues.
misuse_note_en: Do not photograph or post cosplayers without consent. Wearing a costume does not waive ordinary privacy boundaries.

en: ita bag; display bag covered with fan merchandise
example_ja: 推しの缶バッジを並べて痛バッグを作った。
example_en: I made an ita bag by arranging pin badges of my favorite character.
speaker_image: A collector openly displaying many coordinated items for a favorite character or performer.
real_life_use: Common in Japanese fan-goods culture and increasingly known internationally as 'ita bag.' Clear-front bags are popular for protecting the items.
usage_note_en: 痛 is playful slang suggesting an excessive or conspicuous display, related to 痛車. The bag is decorated densely with badges, charms, or cards.
contrast: 痛車: vehicle decorated prominently with character images
推しバッグ: broader bag used to carry or display favorite-related items
example_ja_2: 雨の日は痛バッグにカバーをかけている。
example_en_2: I put a cover over my ita bag on rainy days.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it literally as 'painful bag.' Use established 'ita bag' for informed audiences or explain the display style.

example_ja: 入場特典で丸い缶バッジをもらった。
example_en: I received a round pin-back button as an admission bonus.
speaker_image: A collector, seller, or event attendee referring to a metal-backed pin badge.
real_life_use: Common merchandise vocabulary. English varies: 'pin-back button' in North America and 'badge' in Britain.
usage_note_en: 缶 refers to the thin metal construction, and バッジ to the wearable item. Character art is printed on the front and a pin is attached behind.
contrast: ピンバッジ: usually a small enamel or molded lapel pin
アクリルバッジ: badge made primarily from acrylic
example_ja_2: 缶バッジの裏がさびないように保管する。
example_en_2: I store the pin-back badges so the metal backs do not rust.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 缶 as a can-shaped object. The item is a flat button or badge made with a metal shell.

example_ja: 机に推しのアクリルスタンドを飾っている。
example_en: I display an acrylic standee of my favorite character on my desk.
speaker_image: A fan or retailer referring to a printed acrylic figure mounted upright on a base.
real_life_use: Common merchandise vocabulary, often shortened to アクスタ.
usage_note_en: An アクリルスタンド is a flat printed acrylic piece slotted into a base. It is display merchandise rather than a sculpted figure.
contrast: アクリルキーホルダー: acrylic charm with keychain hardware
フィギュア: three-dimensional figure or statue
example_ja_2: 旅行先でアクスタと風景を一緒に撮った。
example_en_2: I photographed the acrylic standee with the scenery on my trip.
misuse_note_en: Do not call it an acrylic 'stand' alone in English if that suggests only the base; 'standee' identifies the displayed character piece.

example_ja: 会場限定のグッズを売店で買った。
example_en: I bought venue-exclusive merchandise at the shop.
speaker_image: A customer, fan, or seller referring to branded products and accessories.
real_life_use: Very common in entertainment and events. Japanese グッズ is usually plural in sense even without grammatical plural marking.
usage_note_en: Although borrowed from English 'goods,' Japanese グッズ often means merchandise tied to a brand, performer, event, or character.
contrast: 商品: product or item for sale in general
特典: bonus item or benefit supplied under particular conditions
example_ja_2: 公式グッズの一覧が公開された。
example_en_2: The official merchandise lineup was announced.
misuse_note_en: English 'goods' can sound legalistic or generic. Translate fan-related グッズ as 'merchandise' or the specific product type.

example_ja: 限定グッズは一人二点まで購入できる。
example_en: Each person may buy up to two of the limited-edition items.
speaker_image: A seller or fan referring to merchandise restricted by place, time, quantity, or purchase condition.
real_life_use: Common in promotions and events. The basis of limitation should be stated: 会場限定, 期間限定, or 数量限定.
usage_note_en: 限定 only says availability is restricted. It does not automatically mean the item is rare, numbered, or permanently unavailable later.
contrast: 先行販売: sold early before wider release
特典グッズ: bonus merchandise tied to a purchase or campaign
example_ja_2: 通販でも買えるので、会場限定グッズではなかった。
example_en_2: It was also available online, so it was not venue-exclusive merchandise.
misuse_note_en: Do not call an item 'limited edition' without checking what is limited. It may be limited only by sales channel or period.

en: physical disc release; DVD or Blu-ray
example_ja: 配信で見た作品の円盤も予約した。
example_en: I also preordered the series on disc after watching it online.
speaker_image: A fan or industry commentator referring collectively to packaged optical media.
real_life_use: Common fandom shorthand for DVD and Blu-ray releases. Outside this context, 円盤 simply means a circular disk or platter.
usage_note_en: The physical shape gives the slang meaning. 円盤 often appears in discussions of sales, bonuses, box sets, and home-video corrections.
contrast: 配信版: streamed or digitally distributed version
Blu-ray: specific high-definition disc format
example_ja_2: 円盤には放送版で省かれた場面が追加されている。
example_en_2: The disc release adds a scene omitted from the broadcast version.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate fandom 円盤 as a generic 'disk' without context. It usually means a commercial DVD or Blu-ray package.

example_ja: 最終話はテレビ放送の直後に配信される。
example_en: The final episode will stream immediately after the television broadcast.
speaker_image: A platform, creator, or viewer discussing digital delivery of video, audio, or information.
real_life_use: Standard far beyond fandom. It can cover on-demand release, live streaming, music distribution, or sending data.
usage_note_en: 配信 literally distributes content to recipients. ライブ配信 specifies live streaming; 動画配信 can include on-demand video.
contrast: 放送: broadcast through television or radio systems
配布: distribute files or physical materials to recipients
example_ja_2: イベントの様子を公式チャンネルでライブ配信した。
example_en_2: The event was livestreamed on the official channel.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 配信 as live streaming. Check whether the content is live, on demand, downloadable, or simply digitally released.

example_ja: ロゴ入りの公式グッズをオンラインストアで注文した。
example_en: I ordered official logo merchandise from the online store.
speaker_image: A rights holder, seller, or buyer distinguishing authorized merchandise from fan-made or counterfeit items.
real_life_use: Common. Official status should be supported by the manufacturer, license, seller, or rights-holder information.
usage_note_en: 公式グッズ is produced, sold, or licensed by the relevant official organization. It may still be manufactured by a partner company.
contrast: 非公式グッズ: unauthorized or unofficial merchandise
同人グッズ: independently made dōjin merchandise, which may follow fan-work guidelines
example_ja_2: 公式グッズには著作権表示が印刷されていた。
example_en_2: The official merchandise carried a copyright notice.
misuse_note_en: Do not infer official status merely from professional packaging or marketplace claims. Check the rights holder and authorized sales channel.

example_ja: 原作組は登場人物の正体をすでに知っている。
example_en: People familiar with the source material already know the character's identity.
speaker_image: A fan dividing the audience according to prior knowledge of the source work.
real_life_use: Common in adaptation discussions. The group may have read or played some of the source, not necessarily completed it.
usage_note_en: The suffix 組 groups people by route or experience. 原作組 contrasts those who know the source with anime-first or live-action-only viewers.
contrast: アニメ組: viewers following through the anime adaptation
初見勢: people experiencing the story for the first time
example_ja_2: 原作組もネタバレには気をつけている。
example_en_2: Source readers are being careful not to spoil anything either.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 組 as a formal organization, and do not assume every 原作組 knows all later plot developments.

example_ja: 私はアニメ組なので、原作の先の展開は知らない。
example_en: I only follow the anime, so I do not know what happens later in the source material.
speaker_image: A viewer identifying their main route into a story as its anime adaptation.
real_life_use: Common when discussing adaptations and spoiler boundaries. Some アニメ組 later begin the source material.
usage_note_en: 組 groups people by viewing route. アニメ組 generally contrasts with 原作組 rather than claiming the person watches no other media.
contrast: 原作組: audience familiar with the source work
アニメ勢: similar informal label for anime-side viewers
example_ja_2: アニメ組にも分かるように補足説明が入った。
example_en_2: Extra explanation was added so anime-only viewers could follow.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate it as an official 'anime team.' It is an informal audience category and may mean anime-first rather than permanently anime-only.

en: initial sales of the disc release
example_ja: 円盤の初動だけで作品の成功は判断できない。
example_en: Initial disc sales alone cannot determine whether a series succeeded.
speaker_image: A sales watcher or fan discussing the earliest reported sales window for packaged media.
real_life_use: Used in chart and market talk. The exact 初動 period depends on the data source, commonly the first tracked week.
usage_note_en: 初動 means initial movement or early performance. With 円盤, it refers to early DVD/Blu-ray sales, not lifetime units or streaming reach.
contrast: 累計売上: cumulative sales over time
配信再生数: number of streaming plays
example_ja_2: 特典イベントの有無で円盤の初動が変わることもある。
example_en_2: An event bonus can affect a disc release's first-week sales.
misuse_note_en: Always identify the tracker and period when citing a number. 初動 is not a universal fixed metric and excludes later sales.

example_ja: 人気エピソードが新作映像を加えて劇場版になった。
example_en: The popular arc became a theatrical film with newly produced footage.
speaker_image: A studio, cinema, or fan referring to an installment released for theaters.
real_life_use: Common for anime and franchise media. A 劇場版 may be an original story, sequel, adaptation, or compilation.
usage_note_en: 劇場 means theater, and 版 marks a version or edition. The term identifies theatrical release format, not the film's relationship to continuity.
contrast: テレビ版: television version
実写版: live-action version
example_ja_2: 劇場版は来春から全国で公開される。
example_en_2: The theatrical film opens nationwide next spring.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 劇場版 is a remake or compilation. Check whether it is new, continued, retold, or collected material.

example_ja: 新しい店員がイケメンだと話題になっている。
example_en: People are talking about how handsome the new staff member is.
speaker_image: A casual speaker praising a man's looks or, sometimes, admirable conduct.
real_life_use: Widely understood beyond fandom. It is informal and appearance-focused, so direct comments about a stranger can be intrusive.
usage_note_en: Often explained as イケてるメンズ, イケメン primarily means a handsome or attractive man. Figurative uses can praise behavior as cool or considerate.
contrast: 美男子: handsome man, more literary or formal
かっこいい: cool or attractive, usable for people, actions, and things
example_ja_2: 重い荷物を黙って持ってくれるなんて、行動までイケメンだ。
example_en_2: Quietly carrying the heavy bags for us—that was a genuinely classy move.
misuse_note_en: Do not treat it as a neutral demographic label. It evaluates appearance, and applying it publicly can objectify the person.

example_ja: このブランドは淡い色のかわいい系の服が多い。
example_en: This brand carries many clothes in a soft, cute style.
speaker_image: A fan, shopper, or friend classifying an appearance, design, or personality by a cute aesthetic.
real_life_use: Common in fashion, beauty, character, and personality talk. 系 indicates a broad type rather than a strict category.
usage_note_en: かわいい系 groups features associated with cuteness—soft colors, rounded forms, gentle presentation—without saying every item is literally cute.
contrast: きれい系: elegant or beautiful type
かっこいい系: cool or sharp style
example_ja_2: 彼女はかわいい系というより、落ち着いたきれい系だ。
example_en_2: Her style is more calmly elegant than cute.
misuse_note_en: Do not use the label as an objective judgment about someone's identity. It is a loose style category and may not match self-perception.

example_ja: 感情をあまり表に出さないクールキャラだ。
example_en: He is a cool, composed character who rarely shows emotion.
speaker_image: A fan or creator classifying a fictional character as calm, restrained, and stylish.
real_life_use: Mostly a character label, though クール can describe real people. Japanese クール often means emotionally composed as well as fashionable.
usage_note_en: クールキャラ usually speaks and reacts with restraint. The type may be aloof, competent, dryly funny, or secretly caring.
contrast: クーデレ: cool exterior paired with a hidden affectionate side
無口キャラ: character defined specifically by speaking little
example_ja_2: 普段はクールキャラなのに、猫の前では表情が変わる。
example_en_2: She is usually the cool, reserved type, but her expression changes around cats.
misuse_note_en: Do not equate クール with emotionally cold or cruel. It can be positive praise for composure and style.

example_ja: 彼女は自分を腐女子だと公言している。
example_en: She openly identifies herself as a fan of boys' love.
speaker_image: A woman self-identifying, often humorously, as a fan of fictional male–male romance or relationships.
real_life_use: Common within BL fandom, but it can sound derogatory when imposed on someone else. Self-identification is safer than labeling.
usage_note_en: A pun on 婦女子, 腐女子 uses 腐, 'rotten,' as self-deprecating fandom language. It does not mean a female fan of all anime or manga.
contrast: 腐男子: male fan of boys' love
オタク女子: woman deeply interested in a hobby, not specifically BL
example_ja_2: 腐女子向けと決めつけず、作品の対象読者を確認しよう。
example_en_2: Do not assume a work targets BL fans; check its intended audience.
misuse_note_en: Do not call someone 腐女子 merely because she likes male characters. The label concerns BL interest and should not be assigned without consent.

example_ja: 兄は鉄道オタクで、全国の路線に詳しい。
example_en: My brother is a railway enthusiast who knows routes all across Japan.
speaker_image: A speaker describing deep, sustained interest and knowledge in a particular field.
real_life_use: Often neutral or positive as a self-label today, but tone and context can still make it dismissive. Xオタク specifies the interest.
usage_note_en: オタク can mean a devoted hobbyist broadly, not only an anime fan. English 'otaku' is often narrower and more Japan-media-specific.
contrast: マニア: enthusiast or collector with specialized interest
ファン: supporter or admirer, without implying the same depth
example_ja_2: 自分ではオタクというほど詳しくないと思っている。
example_en_2: I do not think I know enough to call myself an otaku.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume the Japanese word always carries the same identity or stigma as English 'geek,' 'nerd,' or imported 'otaku.' Context matters.

example_ja: 自分を陰キャと決めつけて、人付き合いを避けていた。
example_en: He labeled himself an outsider and avoided socializing.
speaker_image: A young speaker sorting self or others into a low-status, quiet, socially awkward character category.
real_life_use: Common youth slang and self-deprecation, but insulting when applied to someone else. It is not equivalent to the neutral personality term 'introvert.'
usage_note_en: Short for 陰気なキャラ. The label bundles perceived quietness, low social status, appearance, and group belonging rather than describing one stable trait.
contrast: 内向的: introverted, neutral descriptive term
ぼっち: someone alone or without companions in a situation
example_ja_2: 静かな人を全員陰キャ扱いするのは失礼だ。
example_en_2: It is rude to label every quiet person as socially inept.
misuse_note_en: Do not teach 陰キャ as a neutral synonym for 'introvert.' It is a reductive social label and may function as an insult.

example_ja: クラスの陽キャたちが文化祭を盛り上げている。
example_en: The class's outgoing social crowd is energizing the school festival.
speaker_image: A young speaker grouping people seen as cheerful, sociable, fashionable, or central to a peer group.
real_life_use: Common as the counterpart to 陰キャ. It may be admiring, teasing, resentful, or reductive depending on tone.
usage_note_en: Short for 陽気なキャラ. The label describes perceived social style and status, not a psychological diagnosis or fixed identity.
contrast: 社交的: sociable, neutral descriptive word
リア充: person whose offline life appears fulfilling, a different axis
example_ja_2: 陽キャに見えても、大人数の集まりが苦手な人はいる。
example_en_2: Some people look highly outgoing but still dislike large gatherings.
misuse_note_en: Do not use 陽キャ and 陰キャ as objective personality tests. They are peer-group labels that flatten individual differences.

example_ja: 職場では趣味を話していない隠れオタクだ。
example_en: I keep my fandom interests private at work.
speaker_image: A fan who enjoys an otaku hobby but chooses not to disclose it in some social settings.
real_life_use: Established casual term. People may conceal an interest because of privacy, stigma, workplace boundaries, or simply personal preference.
usage_note_en: 隠れ means hidden. Unlike 陰キャ, this label concerns disclosure of a hobby, not sociability or personality.
contrast: オープンオタク: person open about their otaku interests
陰キャ: derogatory social-character label, unrelated to whether hobbies are disclosed
example_ja_2: 実は同僚も隠れオタクで、同じ作品が好きだった。
example_en_2: It turned out my coworker was a private fan too, and we liked the same series.
misuse_note_en: Do not infer shame or dishonesty. Keeping a hobby private can be an ordinary boundary, and 隠キャ is not the correct spelling for this idea.

en: person whose offline life seems fulfilling
example_ja: 週末は友達と旅行なんて、リア充っぽい。
example_en: Traveling with friends every weekend—that looks like a pretty full social life.
speaker_image: An online speaker, often jokingly or enviously, describing someone whose life away from the internet appears socially or romantically fulfilling.
real_life_use: Still recognized, though strongly associated with internet-era social comparison. It is not limited to having a romantic partner.
usage_note_en: Short for リアルが充実している, meaning one's 'real' or offline life is fulfilled. The category is based on outward perception and contrast with online life.
contrast: 陽キャ: outgoing social-character label
非リア: person self-described as lacking a fulfilling offline or romantic life
example_ja_2: 恋人がいなくても、仕事と趣味が充実したリア充はいる。
example_en_2: A person can have a fulfilling offline life through work and hobbies without a partner.
misuse_note_en: Do not define リア充 as simply 'someone in a relationship.' It is broader, subjective, and often used with envy or sarcasm.

example_ja: 昼休みはいつも一人で、クラスではぼっちだった。
example_en: I always spent lunch alone and had no group in the class.
speaker_image: A speaker describing themselves or someone else as alone, isolated, or without companions.
real_life_use: Common in self-deprecating compounds such as クリぼっち. Calling another person ぼっち can mock or stigmatize isolation.
usage_note_en: Probably shortened from 独りぼっち. It can describe a temporary situation or an ongoing social position, with tone ranging from humorous to painful.
contrast: 一人: one person or alone, neutral
孤独: loneliness or isolation as an emotional/abstract state
example_ja_2: 今日は友達が休みだから、ぼっちで昼を食べる。
example_en_2: My friend is absent today, so I'm eating lunch alone.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume a person alone is lonely or socially deficient. Use neutral 一人 when no self-deprecating or mocking tone is intended.

example_ja: 恋愛ものでは、主人公を支える友達枠のキャラが好きだ。
example_en: In romance stories, I like the supportive character in the platonic-friend role.
speaker_image: A fan informally assigning a character to a narrative or relationship slot centered on friendship.
real_life_use: Mostly story and casual relationship commentary. 枠 treats roles as slots and can sound impersonal when applied to real people.
usage_note_en: The productive suffix 枠 means a category or allotted position. 友達枠 says a character is framed as a friend rather than the main romantic option.
contrast: 恋愛枠: character positioned as a romantic possibility
親友ポジション: best-friend narrative position
example_ja_2: 最初は友達枠だった人物が、後半で恋愛相手になる。
example_en_2: A character who began in the friend role becomes a love interest later.
misuse_note_en: Do not equate the term mechanically with English 'friend zone,' which often emphasizes rejection and entitlement.

en: foil or secondary suitor used to advance the main romance
example_ja: 彼は主人公の気持ちを自覚させる当て馬として登場する。
example_en: He enters as a secondary suitor whose presence makes the protagonist recognize her feelings.
speaker_image: A fan or critic identifying a character used to provoke jealousy, comparison, or movement in the central romance.
real_life_use: Also used for a person or option serving as a decoy or foil, but it is demeaning when applied to a real romantic partner.
usage_note_en: The original equestrian term referred to a stallion used to stimulate another horse. In stories, the 当て馬 is usually not the final romantic choice.
contrast: 恋敵: romantic rival, who may still have a genuine chance
かませ犬: character used to demonstrate another's strength by losing
example_ja_2: 当て馬だと思われていたキャラが最後に選ばれた。
example_en_2: The character everyone assumed was only the secondary suitor was chosen in the end.
misuse_note_en: Avoid calling a real person an 当て馬. It reduces them to a tool in someone else's relationship and carries a dehumanizing history.

en: go viral; suddenly attract widespread attention
example_ja: 短い感想動画が一晩でバズった。
example_en: The short reaction video went viral overnight.
speaker_image: A creator, marketer, or user describing rapid, large-scale online spread.
real_life_use: Widely used in social media and marketing. The scale is relative, and attention may be positive, negative, or mixed.
usage_note_en: Borrowed from English 'buzz,' バズる is a Japanese verb. Posts, phrases, products, and people can become widely discussed.
contrast: 話題になる: become a topic of conversation, broader and more neutral
炎上する: receive concentrated negative backlash
example_ja_2: バズることより、読者に長く届く記事を作りたい。
example_en_2: I want to make articles with lasting reach rather than merely going viral.
misuse_note_en: Do not treat large view counts alone as proof that something バズった. The word emphasizes sudden spread and social attention.

example_ja: 不用意な投稿が拡散され、企業アカウントが炎上した。
example_en: A careless post spread widely and triggered a backlash against the company account.
speaker_image: A user or journalist describing concentrated online criticism and conflict around a person, organization, or post.
real_life_use: Very common. 炎上 can be serious reputational harm or a smaller platform-specific pile-on; evidence and scale should be stated.
usage_note_en: The fire metaphor presents criticism as rapidly spreading flames. It is not synonymous with any negative comment.
contrast: 荒れる: discussion becomes disorderly or hostile
批判される: receive criticism, without implying viral escalation
example_ja_2: 炎上後に誤情報だったと分かっても、投稿は残り続けた。
example_en_2: Even after the backlash was shown to rest on misinformation, the posts remained online.
misuse_note_en: Do not label ordinary disagreement 炎上 for drama. Verify the scale, concentration, and public spread of the backlash.

example_ja: 最終回の解釈をめぐってコメント欄が荒れた。
example_en: The comment section turned hostile over interpretations of the finale.
speaker_image: A participant or observer describing a space, discussion, weather, or condition becoming disorderly.
real_life_use: Common far beyond the internet: 海が荒れる, 肌が荒れる, and 生活が荒れる use the same verb with different meanings.
usage_note_en: In online contexts, 荒れる means discussion loses order through insults, spam, conflict, or heated repetition. The space is the grammatical subject.
contrast: 炎上する: one target receives widespread backlash
荒らされる: a space is deliberately disrupted by trolls or spam
example_ja_2: 台風で海が荒れている。
example_en_2: The sea is rough because of the typhoon.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 荒れる as an online fight. Identify whether the subject is a forum, weather, skin, lifestyle, or another condition.

example_ja: 発言の一部だけが切り取られ、SNSで叩かれた。
example_en: A fragment of the comment was taken out of context, and the speaker was attacked on social media.
speaker_image: A user or observer describing a person or work becoming the target of harsh repeated criticism.
real_life_use: Common slang extension of 叩く, to hit. It may describe legitimate criticism, harassment, or both, so the evidence matters.
usage_note_en: The passive 叩かれる frames the target as receiving attacks. Online, no physical hitting is implied.
contrast: 批判される: be criticized, neutral about tone
炎上する: backlash grows into a broad public firestorm
example_ja_2: 失敗した選手を必要以上に叩くべきではない。
example_en_2: People should not pile on an athlete excessively for one mistake.
misuse_note_en: Do not use 叩かれた to dismiss all criticism as abuse. Distinguish evidence-based criticism from personal attacks and coordinated harassment.

en: defending camp; those supporting a target
example_ja: 変更を評価する擁護派と、反対派で意見が分かれた。
example_en: Opinion split between those defending the change and those opposing it.
speaker_image: A commentator grouping people who defend a person, decision, or work against criticism.
real_life_use: Common in news and online discussion. 派 marks a camp or tendency, not a formal membership list.
usage_note_en: 擁護 means defend or speak in support, while 派 groups the supporters. The label does not state why they defend the target.
contrast: 反対派: opposing camp
支持者: supporters, often a more stable or affirmative relationship
example_ja_2: 擁護派の中でも、理由は一つではない。
example_en_2: Even among the defenders, people have different reasons.
misuse_note_en: Do not treat 擁護派 as a single coordinated group. It may lump together people with very different arguments.

example_ja: そのゲーム界隈では昔から有名な話だ。
example_en: That story has long been well known in the game's community.
speaker_image: A participant or observer referring loosely to people and discourse around a shared interest.
real_life_use: Now common online. The older spatial meaning is the vicinity or neighborhood around a place.
usage_note_en: 界隈 avoids drawing a hard membership boundary. X界隈 can mean a fandom, professional scene, social-media cluster, or nearby social circle.
contrast: コミュニティ: community, often with clearer participation or structure
業界: industry or professional field
example_ja_2: 駅界隈には小さな飲食店が多い。
example_en_2: There are many small restaurants around the station.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate every 界隈 as 'fandom.' Check whether it means an online scene, professional circle, or literal surrounding area.

en: perceived collective manners or civic conduct
example_ja: 一部の迷惑行為だけでファン全体の民度を決めつけるのは乱暴だ。
example_en: It is unfair to judge an entire fan community by a few people's bad behavior.
speaker_image: A commentator ranking the manners or social behavior of a group, often critically.
real_life_use: Common online but loaded. 民度 historically measures a people's supposed level of civilization, so it can reproduce classist or discriminatory judgments.
usage_note_en: In fandom talk, 民度 usually refers to perceived collective manners: harassment, rule-following, cleanliness, or treatment of outsiders.
contrast: マナー: specific norms of behavior
治安: safety or figurative orderliness of a space
example_ja_2: 民度が低いという言い方では、具体的な問題が見えにくい。
example_en_2: Calling the group 'low-class' hides the specific behavior that needs addressing.
misuse_note_en: Avoid using 民度 as if a diverse group had one moral level. Name the concrete harmful behavior instead of ranking people collectively.

example_ja: 彼はデビュー当時から応援している古参ファンだ。
example_en: He is a long-time fan who has supported them since their debut.
speaker_image: A community member identifying someone who joined or supported a subject relatively early.
real_life_use: Common in fandom, games, organizations, and online communities. It can express respect, self-description, or gatekeeping superiority.
usage_note_en: 古参 means an old or long-serving participant relative to later entrants. The relevant starting point depends on the community.
contrast: 新規: newcomer or recently acquired fan
古株: long-standing member, often in a workplace or organization
example_ja_2: 古参だからといって、新しいファンより偉いわけではない。
example_en_2: Being a long-time fan does not make someone superior to newer fans.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 古参 status proves deeper knowledge or ownership of the community. It can become a gatekeeping label.

example_ja: アニメ化をきっかけに新規勢が増えた。
example_en: The anime adaptation brought in many new fans.
speaker_image: A community member grouping fans who joined relatively recently.
real_life_use: Common online. What counts as 'new' depends entirely on the fandom's timeline and speaker.
usage_note_en: 新規 means new arrival, and 勢 marks a loose cohort. The term can be neutral, welcoming, self-descriptive, or gatekeeping.
contrast: 古参: long-time or early fan
新規ファン: transparent, more neutral expression for a new fan
example_ja_2: 新規勢にも分かる用語集を作った。
example_en_2: We made a glossary that newer fans can understand.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume new fans are less serious or knowledgeable. The label describes entry timing, not value or commitment.

en: leave or move on from a fandom; graduate
example_ja: 受験に集中するため、しばらくアイドルオタクを卒業する。
example_en: I'm stepping away from idol fandom for a while to focus on entrance exams.
speaker_image: A fan framing departure from a hobby, favorite, or activity as graduation.
real_life_use: Common beyond fandom for habits and life stages. In idol groups, 卒業 can also be the formal term for a member's departure.
usage_note_en: The metaphor presents leaving as completing a stage rather than failing. The object is marked with を: Xを卒業する.
contrast: オタクをやめる: directly stop being an otaku
担降り: stop supporting a particular favorite, especially in idol fandom
example_ja_2: 卒業したつもりだったのに、新作を見て戻ってきた。
example_en_2: I thought I had left the fandom, but the new release pulled me back.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume fandom 卒業 is permanent, and distinguish it from a performer's officially announced graduation from a group.

en: get out of a consuming hobby or fandom
example_ja: グッズを減らしても、まだこの沼から抜け出せない。
example_en: Even after reducing my merchandise collection, I still cannot get out of this fandom rabbit hole.
speaker_image: A fan humorously or seriously describing an attempt to reduce involvement in an absorbing interest.
real_life_use: Common metaphor for hobbies and fandom. It can concern time, attention, spending, or emotional investment.
usage_note_en: 沼 is the deep swamp of an interest; 抜け出す means manage to escape. Negative forms are especially common and often affectionate rather than regretful.
contrast: 沼にはまる: become deeply absorbed
卒業する: frame a deliberate departure as completing a stage
example_ja_2: 一度沼から抜け出したのに、映画でまた戻った。
example_en_2: I got out of the fandom once, but the film drew me back in.
misuse_note_en: Avoid trivializing real compulsive spending or distress. The phrase is often playful, but context may describe a genuine need for limits.

en: falling into a fandom rabbit hole
example_ja: ライブ映像一本で、そのバンドに沼落ちした。
example_en: One concert video sent me straight down the rabbit hole for that band.
speaker_image: A fan describing the moment or process of becoming deeply invested in a new interest.
real_life_use: Common online for characters, performers, hobbies, and products. It is usually positive or amused self-description.
usage_note_en: 沼落ち compresses 'falling into the swamp' into a noun or する-verb. A trigger can be marked with 〜で or 〜をきっかけに.
contrast: 沼にはまる: be or become stuck deep in the interest
ハマる: get hooked, broader and less fandom-specific
example_ja_2: 沼落ちのきっかけになった回を今でも覚えている。
example_en_2: I still remember the episode that drew me into the fandom.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 落ち as failure or romantic falling automatically. The compound means deep entry into an interest.

en: more new content than fans can handle; happy overload
example_ja: 新曲と配信とグッズが同日に来て、供給過多だ。
example_en: A new song, stream, and merchandise all arrived on the same day—it's a happy overload.
speaker_image: An excited fan joking that official or fan content is arriving too quickly to process.
real_life_use: Common in fandom. Outside it, 供給過多 is an economic or practical term for oversupply and is often negative.
usage_note_en: 供給 is content supplied to fans; 過多 means excessive quantity. Fandom use often expresses gratitude and overwhelm at once.
contrast: 供給不足: not enough new content
情報過多: too much information, without the fan-content metaphor
example_ja_2: 供給過多で、まだ昨日の動画も見終わっていない。
example_en_2: There is so much new content that I have not even finished yesterday's video.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume positive tone outside fandom. In economics or inventory, 供給過多 simply means excess supply.

en: lack of new content; content drought
example_ja: 半年も新情報がなくて、ファンは供給不足を感じている。
example_en: With no new information for six months, fans are feeling a content drought.
speaker_image: A fan lamenting that little new official or fan content is available.
real_life_use: Common in fandom, while standard contexts use the term for shortages of goods, labor, energy, and other supplies.
usage_note_en: In fan language, 供給 can include art, appearances, announcements, interactions, stories, and merchandise. The source may be official or fan-created.
contrast: 供給過多: happy or practical overload of content
燃料不足: humorous lack of material that sustains a theory or pairing
example_ja_2: 公式の更新が止まり、すっかり供給不足だ。
example_en_2: Official updates have stopped, leaving the fandom starved for content.
misuse_note_en: State what kind of content is missing. 供給不足 alone can sound entitled when creators are resting or under production strain.

example_ja: 購入者限定イベントの応募は今月末までだ。
example_en: Applications for the purchasers-only event close at the end of the month.
speaker_image: An organizer or attendee referring to an event restricted by audience, venue, period, quantity, or eligibility.
real_life_use: Common in marketing. Add the basis of restriction, such as 会員限定, 期間限定, or 地域限定.
usage_note_en: 限定 modifies the event's availability or eligibility. It does not inherently mean 'limited-time' unless time is the stated restriction.
contrast: 期間限定イベント: event available only during a set period
招待制イベント: invitation-only event
example_ja_2: その限定イベントは会員だけが参加できる。
example_en_2: Only members can attend that exclusive event.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 限定イベント automatically as 'limited-time event.' Determine what—time, place, audience, or quantity—is limited.

example_ja: 放送十周年記念で全話が無料配信される。
example_en: All episodes will stream free to commemorate the broadcast's tenth anniversary.
speaker_image: An organization, creator, or fan marking a specified number of years since a launch or event.
real_life_use: Common in entertainment, business, schools, and institutions. The number normally precedes 周年: 五周年記念.
usage_note_en: 周年 counts complete years since an origin point; 記念 marks commemoration. It can modify a product, event, illustration, or campaign.
contrast: 創立記念: commemoration of an organization's founding
生誕祭: birthday celebration for a person, character, or admired figure
example_ja_2: 周年記念グッズの予約が始まった。
example_en_2: Preorders opened for the anniversary merchandise.
misuse_note_en: Do not omit the reference point when it could be unclear. State whether the anniversary marks publication, broadcast, debut, or founding.

en: birthday celebration for a person or character
example_ja: ファンが推しの生誕祭を開き、店内を写真で飾った。
example_en: Fans held a birthday celebration for their favorite and decorated the venue with photos.
speaker_image: Fans or organizers celebrating the birth date of an idol, performer, historical figure, or fictional character.
real_life_use: Common in idol and character fandom, often for fan-organized café events or displays. In other contexts it can sound grander than 誕生日会.
usage_note_en: 生誕 is a formal word for birth; 祭 turns the commemoration into an event. The celebrated subject need not attend or even be a real person.
contrast: 誕生日会: ordinary birthday party
周年記念: anniversary of a work, debut, organization, or event
example_ja_2: キャラクターの生誕祭に合わせて記念イラストが公開された。
example_en_2: A commemorative illustration was released for the character's birthday celebration.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume 生誕祭 is an official event. Fans often organize one independently, so verify organizer and authorization.

kana: たんじょうびいらすと
example_ja: 公式アカウントが主人公の誕生日イラストを公開した。
example_en: The official account posted a birthday illustration of the protagonist.
speaker_image: An artist, rights holder, or fan creating art to mark a person or character's birthday.
real_life_use: Common online. It may be official promotional art or fan art; the phrase alone does not identify the creator.
usage_note_en: 誕生日 specifies the occasion, and イラスト the medium. Common verbs include 描く, 投稿する, and 公開する.
contrast: 記念イラスト: commemorative art for any occasion
ファンアート: fan-created art, regardless of occasion
example_ja_2: 誕生日イラストを本人の公式タグ付きで投稿した。
example_en_2: I posted the birthday tribute art with the person's official hashtag.
misuse_note_en: Do not call an image official merely because it celebrates an official birthday. Check who created and released it.

example_ja: 作品のガイドラインに従ってファンアートを投稿した。
example_en: I posted fan art in accordance with the work's guidelines.
speaker_image: A fan artist or viewer discussing art created by fans around an existing subject.
real_life_use: Widely understood. Fan art may depict fictional characters, performers, games, or other subjects, and rights and publicity issues vary.
usage_note_en: ファンアート identifies the creator's fan relationship, not the medium or legal status. It can be digital, traditional, sculptural, or animated.
contrast: 公式イラスト: art released or authorized officially
二次創作: broader derivative creation including fiction, music, video, and games
example_ja_2: 作者がファンアートを紹介しても、自由利用の許可とは限らない。
example_en_2: An author sharing fan art does not necessarily grant permission for unrestricted reuse.
misuse_note_en: Do not repost, sell, or train on fan art merely because it is publicly visible. Creator rights and the source work's rights both matter.

example_ja: 映画のあと、カフェで二時間も感想戦をした。
example_en: After the film, we spent two hours at a café comparing reactions and interpretations.
speaker_image: Friends, fans, or participants reviewing what happened after a viewing, event, game, or experience.
real_life_use: Originally associated with post-game analysis in shōgi and go, now widely used for informal debriefs after entertainment and events.
usage_note_en: 感想 usually means impressions, but 感想戦 includes replaying moments, analyzing choices, and comparing interpretations—not merely stating likes and dislikes.
contrast: 感想会: meeting focused on sharing impressions
反省会: review centered on mistakes and improvement
example_ja_2: ライブの感想戦まで含めて楽しい一日だった。
example_en_2: The concert and our post-show debrief made the whole day enjoyable.
misuse_note_en: Do not translate 戦 literally as a fight. It is a playful extension of structured post-game review.

example_ja: 好きなキャラは多いけど、最推しは彼女だ。
example_en: I like many characters, but she is my number-one favorite.
speaker_image: A fan ranking one favorite above their other favorites.
real_life_use: Common across character, idol, and performer fandoms. Some fans prefer not to rank their favorites.
usage_note_en: 最 means most or highest; 最推し is the top choice within a person's set of 推し.
contrast: 推し: a favorite one actively supports
単推し: support focused on only one member or target
example_ja_2: 最推しの出番は少ないが、毎週見ている。
example_en_2: My favorite character gets little screen time, but I still watch every week.
misuse_note_en: Do not infer exclusivity. A fan can have a 最推し and several other 推し.

en: supporting the whole group; whole-group fan
example_ja: 一人に決められず、メンバー全員を箱推ししている。
example_en: I cannot choose one member, so I support the group as a whole.
speaker_image: A fan emphasizing affection for an entire group, cast, team, or ensemble.
real_life_use: Common in idol, performer, and ensemble-character fandoms. 箱 refers metaphorically to the group as one package or unit.
usage_note_en: 箱推し does not always mean equal spending or identical affection toward every member. The key is supporting the collective rather than only one target.
contrast: 単推し: focused support for one member
最推し: the fan's top favorite among possible favorites
example_ja_2: 最推しはいるけど、グループとしては箱推しだ。
example_en_2: I have a top favorite, but I support the whole group too.
misuse_note_en: Do not force a binary between 箱推し and individual favorites. Fans often combine both positions.

example_ja: 不便だった機能が全部直って、今回は神アプデだ。
example_en: This update fixed every frustrating feature; it is a fantastic patch.
speaker_image: A player enthusiastically praising a software or game update.
real_life_use: Common in gaming and app communities. It is subjective fan praise and may refer to balance, features, rewards, or fixes.
usage_note_en: 神 is a slang intensifier meaning outstanding; アプデ shortens アップデート. The compound evaluates the update's effect rather than its size.
contrast: 良アプデ: good update, less hyperbolic
改悪: change judged to make a product worse
example_ja_2: 神アプデと言われたが、一部の端末では不具合が出た。
example_en_2: Players praised it as a great update, though it caused bugs on some devices.
misuse_note_en: Do not present 神アプデ as an objective technical verdict. User groups may experience the same update differently.

en: fan who supports the same favorite
example_ja: 会場で同担の人とグッズを交換した。
example_en: At the venue, I traded merchandise with someone who supports the same member.
speaker_image: A fan categorizing another fan by having the same 推し or 担当.
real_life_use: Common especially in idol and character fandoms. The social attitude toward 同担 varies from welcome to avoidance.
usage_note_en: 同 means same and 担 abbreviates 担当, one's supported member in this usage. It describes overlap, not friendship or rivalry by itself.
contrast: 他担: fan whose main favorite is someone else
同担拒否: policy or preference to avoid fans of the same favorite
example_ja_2: 同担歓迎なので、同じ推しの話をしたい。
example_en_2: I welcome fans of the same favorite and would love to talk about them.
misuse_note_en: Do not assume all fandoms use 担当 language or that 同担 automatically means competitor. Usage is community-specific.

en: preference to avoid fans of the same favorite
example_ja: プロフィールに同担拒否と書いて、交流範囲を示している。
example_en: She states in her profile that she does not interact with fans of the same favorite.
speaker_image: A fan communicating that they prefer not to socialize with people who share the same 推し.
real_life_use: Common in some idol and character fandoms. Reasons vary, and the label is a personal boundary rather than a universal rule.
usage_note_en: 拒否 sounds strong, but practical behavior ranges from no interaction to selective avoidance. Profiles may use it to prevent conflict or jealousy.
contrast: 同担歓迎: explicitly welcomes fans of the same favorite
他担: fan of another member or target
example_ja_2: 同担拒否かどうかを相手に確認してからフォローした。
example_en_2: I checked whether they avoid same-favorite fans before following them.
misuse_note_en: Do not mock or pressure someone to change the boundary, but also do not use it to justify harassment or ownership claims over a person.

en: our interpretations match; exactly how I see it
example_ja: その人物の優しさについては、友達と解釈一致だった。
example_en: My friend and I had exactly the same reading of the character's kindness.
speaker_image: A fan delighted that another person, adaptation, or official portrayal matches their understanding.
real_life_use: Common in media discussion and memes. It may refer to characterization, relationships, themes, casting, or design.
usage_note_en: 解釈 is interpretation and 一致 is agreement. As an exclamation, 解釈一致！ means 'Yes—that is exactly right for them.'
contrast: 解釈違い: interpretations differ
公式設定: information explicitly established by the rights holder
example_ja_2: 新衣装が自分の想像と解釈一致でうれしい。
example_en_2: I'm delighted that the new outfit matches exactly how I imagined the character.
misuse_note_en: Agreement does not make an interpretation canon. Distinguish personal 解釈一致 from explicit 公式設定.

en: difference in interpretation; not how I read it
example_ja: 同じ場面でも、二人の関係について解釈違いがあった。
example_en: We interpreted the pair's relationship differently even though we watched the same scene.
speaker_image: A fan marking that another portrayal or reading conflicts with their own.
real_life_use: Common in fan discussion. It can be a calm statement of difference or a sharper rejection, depending on delivery.
usage_note_en: 解釈違い does not necessarily mean one side made a factual error. Many stories support more than one reading.
contrast: 解釈一致: interpretations align
設定ミス: factual inconsistency with established setting
example_ja_2: 解釈違いはあるけど、その絵の技術はすごいと思う。
example_en_2: It is not how I see the character, but the art is technically impressive.
misuse_note_en: Do not use the phrase to disguise harassment of creators or other fans. A different interpretation is not automatically a mistake.

kana: こうしききょうきゅう
en: new official content or material supplied to fans
example_ja: 記念動画と新規イラストで、今日は公式供給が多い。
example_en: Between the anniversary video and new illustration, fans received plenty of official content today.
speaker_image: A fan treating new authorized material as content supplied by the official source.
real_life_use: Common online for announcements, art, dialogue, appearances, merchandise, and relationship material released officially.
usage_note_en: 公式 identifies the rights holder or authorized source; 供給 frames new material as nourishment for fan interest. The phrase is appreciative and informal.
contrast: ファン供給: content created or circulated by fans
公式発表: formal official announcement, narrower and less playful
example_ja_2: 公式供給がなくても、過去の作品を見返して楽しんでいる。
example_en_2: Even without new official content, I enjoy revisiting the older material.
misuse_note_en: Do not treat every rumor, leak, or licensed resale as 公式供給. Verify that the material comes from an authorized source.
